Integrated Model artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal; requirements remain provisional. Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate.

PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY
Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action.

DEPENDENCY MODEL
A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning.

STATE MODEL
Maintain independent fields:
Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided.
Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability.
Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action.
Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion.

REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS
Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan.
Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise.

ADOPTED MODEL REVISION
Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame.

LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK
A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed.

NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS
Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates.

EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING
Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence.
Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted.

NEXT ACTION
Use this model to prepare a small screen outline, matching paper card and dependency questions sheet for review. The proposed interruption and revision activity can demonstrate an interface response without demonstrating learning. A person might select a suggested action because the wording is available, or change direction because the notice improves. Neither establishes retention or transfer. Independent online completion is not the learning target: identifying ambiguity, checking an opportunity, requesting support and declining an unusable route may all be relevant actions.

PROPOSED REQUIREMENT CHANGE
Separate the core planning activity from an optional practice invitation. Do not require revision, explanation or a second task to finish or stop. Keep feedback attached to the explicit choice, with a visible uncertainty statement and correction control. A later transfer inquiry must use a different fictional situation and document which prompts and assistance were available. Do not derive a patron score or readiness judgment from any activity.

Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice with its unexplained “confirm your place” instruction. Offer route preference, availability unknown, none works and undecided choices. Offer one fictional change: “The notice still does not explain confirmation, and help availability is unknown.” Invite keeping, revising, leaving undecided or stopping. STATUS AND BASIS
Provisional integrated Design artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal. Sequence 15 supplies independent preference, provision and session states; sequence 20 separates supported planning from optional practice; sequence 22 adds retention and delegation boundaries. No participant observations, human approval, demonstrated proficiency or empirical success exist. The Understand review gate remains unresolved.

PURPOSE AND DESIGN REVISION
Support an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service, including uncertainty, help-seeking or stopping. Adopt a local deterministic candidate with selected responses only, current-draft memory and no history, analytics, persistent storage, exports or transmissions. This meaningfully revises the earlier optional-written-response design and removes an unnecessary entry point for real details. Preserve dissent about restricted expression: spoken or paper review can surface missing actions without requiring digital notes. Human review may reject this restriction or the tool.

SCREEN OUTLINE AND EXACT CONTENT
Opening text: “Community Drawing Hour is an invented event. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.”
Approach selector: consider online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / undecided. Default: undecided.
Next-action selector: examine the notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / my action is not listed / undecided. Default: undecided. ‘My action is not listed’ is a valid draft; no explanation is required.
‘Describe my draft’ optionally displays fixed text describing the current explicit selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” For an undecided draft: “Your draft is undecided. You may change it, pause or stop.” Changes update any visible description immediately; never leave stale feedback. Do not praise completion or recommend a preferred route.
Keep correction, pause, stop, conceal and clear reachable without completing a plan. No progression lock, compulsory writing, score, deficit label or consequential guidance is permitted.

OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY
Offer two separate invitations: ‘Try a confusing notice’ and ‘Rehearse an interruption.’ Neither is required for assistance or finishing. Confusion text: “The notice still does not explain confirmation, and help availability is unknown.” Interruption text: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue.” These are fictional prompts, not observed events.
Either prompt offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop. Interruption also permits conceal or clear and pauses activity; keeping or resuming requires explicit action. Stopping ends the exercise without judging completion. Clear while paused or stopped preserves that activity state. If a real session loses its draft, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices.

PRIVACY BEHAVIOR
Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and every choice-specific message together. Concealed text: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Offer explicit reveal, clear and stop without revealing choices. Clear removes candidate-held selections, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Confirmation: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Start a new draft only through an explicit action. These behaviors require technical verification.

MATCHING NON-AI MATERIAL
Paper card text: “Invented Community Drawing Hour: morning or afternoon; ‘confirm your place’ is unexplained. No registration occurs; route availability is unknown.” Provide the same approach and next-action choices, plus keep/change/undecided/pause/stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding can conceal paper but is not erasure; agree discreet handling with reviewers. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices are alternatives. Staff availability is not presumed.

REVIEW PACKAGE AND GATES
Prepare this screen outline, paper card and dependency questions: Which routes exist? What assistance boundaries and capacity are realistic? Which language, access and device arrangements are needed? Demand for the tool is also unknown. Proposed human roles are not accepted assignments.
Patron and librarian review must assess framing, refusal, missing actions, privacy wording and workload before approved design. Later technical checks must examine stale output, complete concealment, clear while stopped, storage and transmission boundaries. Human interaction testing must precede any pilot. All checks and field evidence remain pending; retain objections and reasons for revisions.
Learning inquiry is separate, optional and requires review: use another fictional task and document prompts and assistance. Completion, speed or one revised plan cannot establish retention or transfer. Consider familiarity, language demands, fatigue, prompting and service improvements as rival explanations.

NEXT ACTION
Use these paired materials for accountable human review, revise the design from that review, and only then consider an interactive candidate and interaction testing. Review may favor paper, direct assistance, service redesign or no tool.

response.challenged_assumption: Optional practice and complete concealment alone preserve agency or demonstrate learning when choices could still be retained, delegated or copied from prompts.
response.decision: Adopt the integrated Design draft for rehearsal deliberation. Prepare the paired review package and resolve the pending framing, access, privacy and workload gates before treating the design as approved or proceeding toward a pilot.
drawbacks: Selected responses constrain expression and may omit acceptable actions.
Additional controls and explanations introduce reading and navigation effort.
Session-only drafts lose continuity when cleared or the session ends.
flourishing: Agency and dignity: declining routes, assistance, practice or the exercise receives neutral treatment.
Access and belonging: compare screen, paper and spoken participation without privileging independent online completion.
Sustainable workload and learning/transfer: investigate assistance effort and later adaptation separately; neither benefit is established.
human_capabilities: Patrons need accessible selected, spoken or paper participation, with correction, uncertainty and stopping accepted without justification.
Librarians and service owners need bounded review time and authority to reject assistance promises, unclear notices and added workload.
Accountable patron and librarian review must examine framing, access, privacy and dissent; participation and approval remain pending.
response.message: This provisional Design synthesis integrates sequence 15’s dependency and privacy model, sequence 20’s separation of planning from learning inquiry, and sequence 22’s retention and delegation boundaries. The design now uses selected fictional responses and deterministic descriptions, with optional practice and no automatic handoff. These are rehearsal design decisions, not human-approved requirements. Patron and librarian review, technical verification and field evidence remain pending.
objections: Hypothetical patron dissent: “I need direct assistance, and your listed actions do not express my plan.”
Hypothetical librarian dissent: “This planning activity could consume time needed for service assistance.”
Rival explanations include prompt copying, familiarity and clearer wording; difficulty may reflect language, device or service barriers.
risks: Route wording could imply provision or a staff request despite disclaimers.
Concealed content could remain exposed through summaries or interruption output.
An improved draft could be mistaken for learning despite prompting or clearer wording.
system_capabilities: Use fixed fictional choices and deterministic feedback; no free text, persistent storage, tracking, transmission, exports or automatic handoffs.
Keep preference, unknown provision, next action, visibility and activity separate; allow correction, undecided choices and explicit stopping.
Conceal every plan-bearing display; clear candidate-held content with scope confirmation and preserve paused or stopped activity.
tradeoffs: Prompts support immediate planning but obscure what transfers without support.
Concealment preserves a draft; clearing sacrifices continuity for discretion.
Staff conversation may reduce reading demands while adding workload and reducing privacy.

Opening text: “Community Drawing Hour is an invented event. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.”
Approach selector: consider online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / undecided. Default: undecided.
Next-action selector: examine the notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / my action is not listed / undecided. Default: undecided. ‘My action is not listed’ is a valid draft; no explanation is required.
‘Describe my draft’ optionally displays fixed text describing the current explicit selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” For an undecided draft: “Your draft is undecided. You may change it, pause or stop.” Changes update any visible description immediately; never leave stale feedback. Do not praise completion or recommend a preferred route.
Keep correction, pause, stop, conceal and clear reachable without completing a plan. No progression lock, compulsory writing, score, deficit label or consequential guidance is permitted.

OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY
Offer two separate invitations: ‘Try a confusing notice’ and ‘Rehearse an interruption.’ Neither is required for assistance or finishing. Confusion text: “The notice still does not explain confirmation, and help availability is unknown.” Interruption text: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue.” These are fictional prompts, not observed events.
Either prompt offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop. Interruption also permits conceal or clear and pauses activity; keeping or resuming requires explicit action. Stopping ends the exercise without judging completion. Clear while paused or stopped preserves that activity state. If a real session loses its draft, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices.

PRIVACY BEHAVIOR
Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and every choice-specific message together. Concealed text: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Offer explicit reveal, clear and stop without revealing choices. Clear removes candidate-held selections, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Confirmation: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Start a new draft only through an explicit action. These behaviors require technical verification.

MATCHING NON-AI MATERIAL
Paper card text: “Invented Community Drawing Hour: morning or afternoon; ‘confirm your place’ is unexplained. No registration occurs; route availability is unknown.” Provide the same approach and next-action choices, plus keep/change/undecided/pause/stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding can conceal paper but is not erasure; agree discreet handling with reviewers. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices are alternatives. Staff availability is not presumed.

REVIEW PACKAGE AND GATES
Prepare this screen outline, paper card and dependency questions: Which routes exist? What assistance boundaries and capacity are realistic? Which language, access and device arrangements are needed? Demand for the tool is also unknown. Proposed human roles are not accepted assignments.
Patron and librarian review must assess framing, refusal, missing actions, privacy wording and workload before approved design. Later technical checks must examine stale output, complete concealment, clear while stopped, storage and transmission boundaries. Human interaction testing must precede any pilot. All checks and field evidence remain pending; retain objections and reasons for revisions.
Learning inquiry is separate, optional and requires review: use another fictional task and document prompts and assistance. Completion, speed or one revised plan cannot establish retention or transfer. Consider familiarity, language demands, fatigue, prompting and service improvements as rival explanations.

NEXT ACTION
Use these paired materials for accountable human review, revise the design from that review, and only then consider an interactive candidate and interaction testing. Integrated Model artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal; requirements remain provisional. Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate.

PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY
Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action.

DEPENDENCY MODEL
A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning.

STATE MODEL
Maintain independent fields:
Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided.
Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability.
Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action.
Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion.

REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS
Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan.
Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise.

ADOPTED MODEL REVISION
Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame.

LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK
A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed.

NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS
Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates.

EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING
Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence.
Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted.

NEXT ACTION

PROBLEM FRAME
Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping.

ADOPTED REVISION
The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. These are working requirements awaiting human review, not approved commitments.

FICTIONAL REVIEW MATERIAL
Exercise text: “Imagine a made-up library event called Community Drawing Hour. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.”

Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline:

Examine what appears after interruption and session ending. Wording, languages, keyboard access and other participation arrangements require review. Compare the candidate with the same paper card and an ordinary conversation with available staff. Review may favor either alternative or reject the workbench. Expert draft for public deliberation, not approved requirements. This lifecycle is a rehearsal. The seed supplies the invented Community Drawing Hour task and privacy restrictions. Sequence 4 raises route reality, privacy and staff capacity; sequence 6 adds uncertainty, refusal and stopping; sequence 8 incorporates these into the Understand artifact. No participant observations, human approval or field evidence exist. Modeling here does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate.

COUPLED SYSTEM MODEL
Actors are the patron, available librarian or volunteer, service owner and shared-device operator. Their participation and capacity are unknown. The candidate can describe a fictional plan; it cannot supply service access, reserve staff time, register attendance or establish readiness.

Keep four independent aspects of state:
• Preference: online, check paper, check staffed assistance, unknown, none works, or stop.
• Provision: unknown in this rehearsal. Choosing a route never changes its availability.
• Next action: selected fictional action or undecided; no written explanation required.
• Session: visible, concealed, interrupted or cleared. Session state must not infer patron intention.

This separation exposes the dependency between a desired action and an opportunity to perform it. “Ask staff” remains conditional on assistance being available. “Check paper” does not establish that paper registration exists. An undecided action remains a valid draft.

REQUIREMENT CHALLENGE AND REVISION
The current framing distinguishes concealment from clearing but does not specify every place a plan may appear. Proposed model requirement: concealment must hide notes, route selections and derived descriptive feedback together. Revealing them requires an explicit action. The concealed view must state that fictional content remains in the session. Otherwise, hiding a note while leaving its summary visible defeats the intended discretion.

Recovery must also distinguish an interrupted plan from a completed or abandoned plan. An interruption prompt must offer keep, revise, clear or stop without requiring reasons. No automatic resumption, staff request or recreation of lost content is permitted. If content is lost, describe that condition and permit a fresh undecided draft or stopping; do not reconstruct an inferred plan.

REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS
Selection or correction changes only the explicit draft choices and their descriptive output. A confusing “confirm your place” instruction may lead to asking what it means, checking another route, leaving the action undecided or stopping. It must not trigger invented procedural advice.

Conceal hides every plan-bearing display while retaining current-session content. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and derived output, then visibly confirms its scope. DESIGN CHALLENGE
The proposed interruption and revision activity can demonstrate an interface response without demonstrating learning. A person might select a suggested action because the wording is available, or change direction because the notice improves. Neither establishes retention or transfer. Independent online completion is not the learning target: identifying ambiguity, checking an opportunity, requesting support and declining an unusable route may all be relevant actions.

PROPOSED REQUIREMENT CHANGE
Separate the core planning activity from an optional practice invitation. Do not require revision, explanation or a second task to finish or stop. Keep feedback attached to the explicit choice, with a visible uncertainty statement and correction control. A later transfer inquiry must use a different fictional situation and document which prompts and assistance were available. Do not derive a patron score or readiness judgment from any activity.

CORE SCREEN AND PAPER CARD
Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice with its unexplained “confirm your place” instruction. Offer route preference, availability unknown, none works and undecided choices. Permit a selected next action, an optional fictional response, or no action. Show concise descriptive feedback only when wanted. Keep revise, pause, stop, conceal and clear available as specified in sequence 15.

Example feedback: “Your draft selects asking what ‘confirm your place’ means if help is available. Help availability remains unknown. You may keep, change or leave this action undecided.” Feedback describes the draft; it does not certify that the action is feasible or that the patron understands it. Conceal this output with every other plan-bearing display.

OPTIONAL DELIBERATE PRACTICE
Offer one fictional change: “The notice still does not explain confirmation, and help availability is unknown.” Invite keeping, revising, leaving undecided or stopping. The practice focus is reconsidering a plan when a dependency is unresolved. Show no preferred route or praise for continuing. An optional selected response can identify what changed; explanation is never mandatory. Repetition is an invitation, not a prerequisite for assistance.

RETENTION AND TRANSFER INQUIRY — PROPOSED ONLY
If separately reviewed and voluntarily undertaken, use a later fictional activity without displaying the earlier plan. For example, an invented craft-session notice offers two times but gives contradictory confirmation instructions. Initially omit copied next-action examples, while keeping requested support available. Examine whether a reviewer identifies the uncertainty or chooses an acceptable response, including help-seeking or stopping. Record whether examples, explanation or assistance were supplied. This inquiry needs no personal records, contact details or stored patron history.

A later response could inform retention of the planning approach; adaptation to changed task features could inform transfer. Neither can be established by one completed exercise. An absent response supplies no evidence of inability. Reviewers must consider language demands, familiarity, prompting, fatigue and unavailable opportunities alongside any learning explanation. Appropriate delay, task comparability and acceptable review burden remain unknown.

NON-AI AND SERVICE ALTERNATIVES
Use the same card on paper or discuss the notice with available staff. Paper needs readable wording and discreet handling. Compare these approaches with clarifying the service notice itself; removing ambiguity may eliminate the need for practice. Retain objections to adding another learning task.

Prepare the paired screen outline and paper card, exact feedback examples, and a separate optional inquiry sheet identifying support conditions and rival explanations. RESPONSIBILITY CHALLENGE
Display privacy does not settle collection, retention or delegation. An interface could conceal a plan while recording route choices, revisions, hesitation or help requests elsewhere. Likewise, selecting “check staffed help” must not silently create a handoff, imply consent to disclosure or reserve librarian time. These are design risks to examine, not reported incidents.

PROPOSED DESIGN REVISION
Make the small candidate a local, deterministic fictional planning tool. Use fixed descriptive templates rather than model-generated advice. Store only the current draft in temporary session memory; propose no analytics, interaction histories, persistent storage, exports or transmissions. Do not retain previous choices for a learning profile. Prefer selected responses for the first candidate, with no free-text notes field. This removes an unnecessary opportunity to enter real details while retaining undecided, none-works and stop choices. Patron review may challenge the restriction on expression.

An assistance selection changes only the fictional draft. Display: “Your draft selects checking whether staffed help is available. Availability is unknown. No request has been sent.” Do not contact staff, allocate work or infer permission. The patron decides whether to approach available assistance outside the candidate. No action certifies real registration, readiness, skill or consent.

SCREEN OUTLINE FOR REVIEW
Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice and its unexplained “confirm your place” instruction. Offer approach and next-action selections, including uncertainty and no action. Show a short description of the explicit draft with availability unknown. Place change, pause, stop, conceal and clear controls where they remain reachable without completing the exercise. Optional practice is separate and never unlocks assistance.

Conceal must hide selections, feedback and any other plan-bearing display, including choice-specific interruption messages. The concealed view explains that fictional content remains and offers explicit reveal or clear. Clear removes candidate-held choices and derived descriptions, confirms its scope, and preserves a stopped state. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Do not automatically recreate a cleared draft.

CORRECTION AND HUMAN ACCOUNTABILITY
Patrons control draft choices; correction requires no explanation. Feedback must acknowledge an undecided draft without steering toward completion. Librarian review must define assistance boundaries and assess workload; service-information questions require an accountable human owner rather than invented tool answers. These responsibilities are proposed roles, not assigned duties or accepted commitments. Human review must be able to reject the tool, its practice component or a particular route description. Preserve dissent and unresolved issues without declaring consensus.

NON-AI OPTION
Prepare a paper card with the same fictional notice, unknown availability, next-action, correction and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Review discreet paper handling and spoken participation. Clarifying the service notice may remove the need for a planning exercise altogether.

Propose technical checks using fictional choices: do correction and clearing remove stale feedback; does concealment cover interruption output; does clear while stopped remain stopped; do storage and network inspection support the proposed no-retention/no-transmission boundary? These are planned checks, not verified results.

Patron and librarian review should examine whether route wording implies provision, whether refusal is easy, whether selected responses constrain expression, and whether the exercise displaces useful assistance. Unknowns include shared-device behavior, access and language arrangements, staffing capacity and whether patrons want the candidate. Apparent ease could reflect familiarity or prompting; difficulty could reflect service ambiguity or device conditions. Field evidence remains pending.

Provisional integrated Design artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal. Sequence 15 supplies independent preference, provision and session states; sequence 20 separates supported planning from optional practice; sequence 22 adds retention and delegation boundaries. No participant observations, human approval, demonstrated proficiency or empirical success exist. The Understand review gate remains unresolved.

PURPOSE AND DESIGN REVISION
Support an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service, including uncertainty, help-seeking or stopping. Adopt a local deterministic candidate with selected responses only, current-draft memory and no history, analytics, persistent storage, exports or transmissions. This meaningfully revises the earlier optional-written-response design and removes an unnecessary entry point for real details. Preserve dissent about restricted expression: spoken or paper review can surface missing actions without requiring digital notes. Human review may reject this restriction or the tool.

SCREEN OUTLINE AND EXACT CONTENT
Opening text: “Community Drawing Hour is an invented event. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.”
Approach selector: consider online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / undecided. Default: undecided.
Next-action selector: examine the notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / my action is not listed / undecided. Default: undecided. ‘My action is not listed’ is a valid draft; no explanation is required.
‘Describe my draft’ optionally displays fixed text describing the current explicit selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” For an undecided draft: “Your draft is undecided. You may change it, pause or stop.” Changes update any visible description immediately; never leave stale feedback. Do not praise completion or recommend a preferred route.
Keep correction, pause, stop, conceal and clear reachable without completing a plan. No progression lock, compulsory writing, score, deficit label or consequential guidance is permitted.

OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY
Offer two separate invitations: ‘Try a confusing notice’ and ‘Rehearse an interruption.’ Neither is required for assistance or finishing. Confusion text: “The notice still does not explain confirmation, and help availability is unknown.” Interruption text: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue.” These are fictional prompts, not observed events.
Either prompt offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop. Interruption also permits conceal or clear and pauses activity; keeping or resuming requires explicit action. Stopping ends the exercise without judging completion. Clear while paused or stopped preserves that activity state. If a real session loses its draft, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices.

PRIVACY BEHAVIOR
Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and every choice-specific message together. Concealed text: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Offer explicit reveal, clear and stop without revealing choices. Clear removes candidate-held selections, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Confirmation: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Start a new draft only through an explicit action. These behaviors require technical verification.

MATCHING NON-AI MATERIAL
Paper card text: “Invented Community Drawing Hour: morning or afternoon; ‘confirm your place’ is unexplained. No registration occurs; route availability is unknown.” Provide the same approach and next-action choices, plus keep/change/undecided/pause/stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding can conceal paper but is not erasure; agree discreet handling with reviewers. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices are alternatives. Staff availability is not presumed.

REVIEW PACKAGE AND GATES
Prepare this screen outline, paper card and dependency questions: Which routes exist? What assistance boundaries and capacity are realistic? Which language, access and device arrangements are needed? Demand for the tool is also unknown. Proposed human roles are not accepted assignments.
Patron and librarian review must assess framing, refusal, missing actions, privacy wording and workload before approved design. Later technical checks must examine stale output, complete concealment, clear while stopped, storage and transmission boundaries. Human interaction testing must precede any pilot. All checks and field evidence remain pending; retain objections and reasons for revisions.
Learning inquiry is separate, optional and requires review: use another fictional task and document prompts and assistance. Completion, speed or one revised plan cannot establish retention or transfer. Consider familiarity, language demands, fatigue, prompting and service improvements as rival explanations.

NEXT ACTION
Use these paired materials for accountable human review, revise the design from that review, and only then consider an interactive candidate and interaction testing. STATUS AND BASIS
Expert scenario draft for public deliberation in a rehearsal, not an approved requirement. Sequence 15 separates visibility, content and activity; sequence 24 specifies reachable conceal, clear and stop controls but does not define layout or focus behavior. No participant observations, technical findings, approvals or field results exist.

ONE HYPOTHETICAL EVENT
Imagine an adult exploring the invented Community Drawing Hour on a shared computer using keyboard navigation and screen magnification. A plausible implementation places privacy controls after the notice, selectors and optional description. When the fictional interruption occurs, only the enlarged planning content is in view. The patron cannot locate conceal or clear promptly, and staff assistance is unavailable. This is an invented event exposing a design gap, not a report about a person or a tested interface.

CHALLENGED ASSUMPTION
Making controls available somewhere without a progression lock makes privacy and stopping practically accessible during an interruption.

REQUESTED REQUIREMENT CHANGE
Revise Design before implementing its screen outline. Specify a short, clearly labeled conceal/clear/stop strip before planning content in keyboard order and available across active, paused and stopped states. Its layout must keep the controls discoverable at magnification settings agreed through human review, without requiring traversal of draft choices or horizontal scrolling. Do not assume a particular device, shortcut convention or staff intervention.

Conceal and clear must move keyboard focus to a neutral status that reveals no choices. Conceal retains the draft and requires explicit reveal; clear removes candidate-held content and preserves paused or stopped activity. Retain sequence 24's limits on browser and device records. This revises control placement and focus requirements rather than merely adding an interruption story.

PROPOSED REVIEW CHECKS — NO RESULTS
Using fictional selections only, examine whether keyboard and magnified users can locate privacy controls from each planning state, whether reflow leaves choices exposed, and whether focus remains understandable after conceal or clear. Technical verification and patron interaction review remain pending. Timing or successful control activation must not become patron scores or evidence of learning transfer.

drawbacks: Persistent controls occupy limited screen space.
Additional navigation instructions can increase reading effort.
Device and assistive-technology behavior still require verification.
flourishing: Agency and dignity: privacy and stopping must remain usable under interruption pressure.

human_capabilities: Patrons need keyboard and magnified access to conceal, clear and stop without justification.

response.message: Hypothetical Design challenge: during a shared-computer interruption, a patron using keyboard navigation and screen magnification cannot locate conceal or clear because those controls sit beyond the enlarged planning content. Staff assistance is unavailable. Sequence 24 requires reachable controls but leaves their placement and focus behavior unspecified. Propose a concrete access requirement; this is an expert draft, with no observed incident, approval or field evidence.
objections: Hypothetical patron dissent: “A conceal button does not help if I cannot find it when someone approaches.”
Dissent: a persistent control strip may crowd the task; paper or direct assistance may be preferable.
Rival explanations include unfamiliar labels, layout complexity and session pressure; preferred magnification, device behavior and assistance capacity remain unknown.
risks: A nominally reachable control may be practically inaccessible during interruption.
Reflow or focus changes could leave selections exposed.
Unavailable assistance could turn recovery into additional patron effort.
system_capabilities: Place a clearly labeled privacy and stop strip before planning content in keyboard order; keep it available in active, paused and stopped states.
Require layouts at human-reviewed magnification settings to expose those controls without traversing choice-specific content or horizontal scrolling.
After conceal or clear, move focus to a neutral status and expose no draft choices through the focused control or status.
tradeoffs: Keeping privacy controls prominent reduces space for task content.
A short control strip improves discovery but must retain understandable labels.
Clearing protects discretion while sacrificing draft continuity.

Provisional integrated Design artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal. Sequence 15 supplies independent preference, provision and session states; sequence 20 separates supported planning from optional practice; sequence 22 adds retention and delegation boundaries. No participant observations, human approval, demonstrated proficiency or empirical success exist. The Understand review gate remains unresolved.

PURPOSE AND DESIGN REVISION
Support an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service, including uncertainty, help-seeking or stopping. Adopt a local deterministic candidate with selected responses only, current-draft memory and no history, analytics, persistent storage, exports or transmissions. This meaningfully revises the earlier optional-written-response design and removes an unnecessary entry point for real details. Preserve dissent about restricted expression: spoken or paper review can surface missing actions without requiring digital notes. Human review may reject this restriction or the tool.

SCREEN OUTLINE AND EXACT CONTENT
Opening text: “Community Drawing Hour is an invented event. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.”
Approach selector: consider online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / undecided. Default: undecided.
Next-action selector: examine the notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / my action is not listed / undecided. Default: undecided. ‘My action is not listed’ is a valid draft; no explanation is required.
‘Describe my draft’ optionally displays fixed text describing the current explicit selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” For an undecided draft: “Your draft is undecided. You may change it, pause or stop.” Changes update any visible description immediately; never leave stale feedback. Do not praise completion or recommend a preferred route.
Keep correction, pause, stop, conceal and clear reachable without completing a plan. No progression lock, compulsory writing, score, deficit label or consequential guidance is permitted.

OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY
Offer two separate invitations: ‘Try a confusing notice’ and ‘Rehearse an interruption.’ Neither is required for assistance or finishing. Confusion text: “The notice still does not explain confirmation, and help availability is unknown.” Interruption text: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue.” These are fictional prompts, not observed events.
Either prompt offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop. Interruption also permits conceal or clear and pauses activity; keeping or resuming requires explicit action. Stopping ends the exercise without judging completion. Clear while paused or stopped preserves that activity state. If a real session loses its draft, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices.

PRIVACY BEHAVIOR
Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and every choice-specific message together. Concealed text: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Offer explicit reveal, clear and stop without revealing choices. Clear removes candidate-held selections, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Confirmation: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Start a new draft only through an explicit action. These behaviors require technical verification.

MATCHING NON-AI MATERIAL
Paper card text: “Invented Community Drawing Hour: morning or afternoon; ‘confirm your place’ is unexplained. No registration occurs; route availability is unknown.” Provide the same approach and next-action choices, plus keep/change/undecided/pause/stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding can conceal paper but is not erasure; agree discreet handling with reviewers. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices are alternatives. Staff availability is not presumed.

REVIEW PACKAGE AND GATES
Prepare this screen outline, paper card and dependency questions: Which routes exist? What assistance boundaries and capacity are realistic? Which language, access and device arrangements are needed? Demand for the tool is also unknown. Proposed human roles are not accepted assignments.
Patron and librarian review must assess framing, refusal, missing actions, privacy wording and workload before approved design. Later technical checks must examine stale output, complete concealment, clear while stopped, storage and transmission boundaries. Human interaction testing must precede any pilot. All checks and field evidence remain pending; retain objections and reasons for revisions.
Learning inquiry is separate, optional and requires review: use another fictional task and document prompts and assistance. Completion, speed or one revised plan cannot establish retention or transfer. Consider familiarity, language demands, fatigue, prompting and service improvements as rival explanations.

NEXT ACTION
Use these paired materials for accountable human review, revise the design from that review, and only then consider an interactive candidate and interaction testing. Review may favor paper, direct assistance, service redesign or no tool.","prototype_html":"","title":"Design synthesis: a bounded fictional planning workbench and paper comparison"},"content_hash":"c1f11d79a9dc4c15a53faa41af6996ccb6d6752d1fe9a1eb7e5cc393205b35c2","id":"design","parent_revision":null,"revision":1,"trigger_seq":24},"model":{"content":{"body":"STATUS AND BASIS
Integrated Model artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal; requirements remain provisional. Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate.

PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY
Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action.

DEPENDENCY MODEL
A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning.

STATE MODEL
Maintain independent fields:
Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided.
Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability.
Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action.
Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion.

REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS
Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan.
Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise.

ADOPTED MODEL REVISION
Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame.

LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK
A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed.

NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS
Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates.

EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING
Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence.
Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted.

NEXT ACTION
Use this model to prepare a small screen outline, matching paper card and dependency questions sheet for review. Keep any subsequent Design work explicitly provisional until the unresolved human gate is met.","prototype_html":"","title":"Model synthesis: supported choice, bounded assistance and revisable plans"},"content_hash":"20628f8a6e48e1f171f619d20e4a92c67f0dc7e5298c432211ff53d3709df9b5","id":"model","parent_revision":null,"revision":1,"trigger_seq":15},"understand":{"content":{"body":"STATUS AND BASIS

Sequence 6 challenges the assumption that three offered routes constitute meaningful choice. The seed supplies the fictional task and restrictions. No participant observations, human approvals or field results exist.

PROBLEM FRAME
Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping.

ADOPTED REVISION
The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. These are working requirements awaiting human review, not approved commitments.

FICTIONAL REVIEW MATERIAL
Exercise text: “Imagine a made-up library event called Community Drawing Hour. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.”

Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline:
• Approach: online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / pause or stop.
• Next action: examine the fictional notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / leave undecided / stop. A different fictional action may be expressed, but writing is optional.
• Change prompt: “The shared computer session ends before you continue, or the instruction remains confusing. Keep, change or abandon your plan.” Do not require recovery or an explanation.
• Feedback example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability remains unknown. You can change or stop this plan.” Feedback describes explicit choices only; it cannot establish access, readiness, consent, skill or transfer.

PRIVACY AND ACCESS BOUNDARIES
Use no real passwords, identifiers, contact details, account information or service records. Concealment must explain that fictional notes remain in the current session. Clearing must remove candidate-held notes and visibly confirm removal; it must not promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Examine what appears after interruption and session ending. Wording, languages, keyboard access and other participation arrangements require review. Paper also needs readable wording, physical access and discreet handling.

COMPARISON AND OPEN QUESTIONS
Compare the candidate with the same paper card and an ordinary conversation with available staff. Review may favor either alternative or reject the workbench. Unknowns include actual route availability, assistance boundaries, staff capacity, language needs, shared-device behavior and whether another planning task is wanted. Preserve objections even if other reviewers favor the candidate.

EVIDENCE PLAN — ALL PENDING
Proposed review questions: Can reviewers identify an acceptable action, including no action? Do route labels imply unavailable provision? Can they revise, conceal, clear and stop with understandable consequences? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens does each approach introduce? Use fictional content only and retain contrary accounts. Difficulty could reflect instructions or unavailable opportunities; apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity. Later transfer would need separate evidence in another fictional task and cannot be inferred from completion here.

NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE
Prepare the paired paper card and screen outline from these working requirements, plus a route-and-assistance questions sheet. Then arrange patron and librarian review of the problem framing, refusal paths, access arrangements, privacy wording and workload boundaries. Record proposed changes and unresolved dissent without declaring consensus. Advancement requires accountable human review of this framing; any interactive candidate subsequently requires human review and interaction testing before a pilot. PROBLEM FRAME
Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping.

ADOPTED REVISION
The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. These are working requirements awaiting human review, not approved commitments.

FICTIONAL REVIEW MATERIAL
Exercise text: “Imagine a made-up library event called Community Drawing Hour. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.”

Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline:
• Approach: online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / pause or stop.
• Next action: examine the fictional notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / leave undecided / stop. A different fictional action may be expressed, but writing is optional.
• Change prompt: “The shared computer session ends before you continue, or the instruction remains confusing. Keep, change or abandon your plan.” Do not require recovery or an explanation.
• Feedback example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability remains unknown. You can change or stop this plan.” Feedback describes explicit choices only; it cannot establish access, readiness, consent, skill or transfer.

PRIVACY AND ACCESS BOUNDARIES
Use no real passwords, identifiers, contact details, account information or service records. Concealment must explain that fictional notes remain in the current session. Clearing must remove candidate-held notes and visibly confirm removal; it must not promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Examine what appears after interruption and session ending. Wording, languages, keyboard access and other participation arrangements require review. Paper also needs readable wording, physical access and discreet handling.

COMPARISON AND OPEN QUESTIONS
Compare the candidate with the same paper card and an ordinary conversation with available staff. Review may favor either alternative or reject the workbench. Unknowns include actual route availability, assistance boundaries, staff capacity, language needs, shared-device behavior and whether another planning task is wanted. Preserve objections even if other reviewers favor the candidate.

EVIDENCE PLAN — ALL PENDING
Proposed review questions: Can reviewers identify an acceptable action, including no action? Do route labels imply unavailable provision? Can they revise, conceal, clear and stop with understandable consequences? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens does each approach introduce? Use fictional content only and retain contrary accounts. Difficulty could reflect instructions or unavailable opportunities; apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity. Later transfer would need separate evidence in another fictional task and cannot be inferred from completion here.

COUPLED SYSTEM MODEL
Actors are the patron, available librarian or volunteer, service owner and shared-device operator. Their participation and capacity are unknown. The candidate can describe a fictional plan; it cannot supply service access, reserve staff time, register attendance or establish readiness.

Keep four independent aspects of state:
• Preference: online, check paper, check staffed assistance, unknown, none works, or stop.
• Provision: unknown in this rehearsal. Choosing a route never changes its availability.
• Next action: selected fictional action or undecided; no written explanation required.
• Session: visible, concealed, interrupted or cleared. Session state must not infer patron intention.

This separation exposes the dependency between a desired action and an opportunity to perform it. “Ask staff” remains conditional on assistance being available. “Check paper” does not establish that paper registration exists. An undecided action remains a valid draft.

REQUIREMENT CHALLENGE AND REVISION
The current framing distinguishes concealment from clearing but does not specify every place a plan may appear. Proposed model requirement: concealment must hide notes, route selections and derived descriptive feedback together. Revealing them requires an explicit action. The concealed view must state that fictional content remains in the session. Otherwise, hiding a note while leaving its summary visible defeats the intended discretion.

Recovery must also distinguish an interrupted plan from a completed or abandoned plan. An interruption prompt must offer keep, revise, clear or stop without requiring reasons. No automatic resumption, staff request or recreation of lost content is permitted. If content is lost, describe that condition and permit a fresh undecided draft or stopping; do not reconstruct an inferred plan.

REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS
Selection or correction changes only the explicit draft choices and their descriptive output. A confusing “confirm your place” instruction may lead to asking what it means, checking another route, leaving the action undecided or stopping. It must not trigger invented procedural advice.

Conceal hides every plan-bearing display while retaining current-session content. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and derived output, then visibly confirms its scope. That confirmation must not promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Stop must end the exercise without a completion judgment and leave conceal/clear controls accessible while content remains. Session-ending behavior needs technical verification with fictional data.

NON-TRAINING LEVERS AND COMPARISON
Investigate clearer service notices, verified route descriptions, assistance boundaries and shared-device session arrangements before proposing patron training. These changes depend on accountable service owners and library review; they are not assumed resources. Compare the candidate with the same paper planning card and an ordinary conversation when staff are available. Paper requires readable wording and discreet handling, and can be rejected too.

UNKNOWN DEPENDENCIES AND EVIDENCE
Route existence, staffing windows, assistance effort, language arrangements, accessibility needs and device behavior are unresolved. Proposed fictional interaction checks should examine concealment of all displays, correction after confusion, interruption without staff, clear followed by a fresh session, and stopping with an undecided plan. These are proposed checks, not results. Field evidence remains pending. Completion, speed and polished wording cannot establish agency, access, proficiency or transfer.

Use this model to prepare a small state-transition outline and paired paper card for patron and librarian review. Retain objections about extra effort and staff burden. PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY
Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action.

DEPENDENCY MODEL
A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning.

STATE MODEL
Maintain independent fields:
Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided.
Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability.
Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action.
Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion.

REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS
Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan.
Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise.

ADOPTED MODEL REVISION
Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame.

LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK
A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed.

NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS
Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates.

EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING
Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence.

Expert draft for public deliberation, not approved requirements. This lifecycle is a rehearsal. Sequence 8 makes uncertainty and stopping legitimate; sequence 13 requires complete concealment; sequence 15 distinguishes preference from provision and identifies learning as a hypothesis. No participant observations, demonstrated proficiency, human approval or field evidence exist.

DESIGN CHALLENGE
The proposed interruption and revision activity can demonstrate an interface response without demonstrating learning. A person might select a suggested action because the wording is available, or change direction because the notice improves. Neither establishes retention or transfer. Independent online completion is not the learning target: identifying ambiguity, checking an opportunity, requesting support and declining an unusable route may all be relevant actions.

PROPOSED REQUIREMENT CHANGE
Separate the core planning activity from an optional practice invitation. Do not require revision, explanation or a second task to finish or stop. Keep feedback attached to the explicit choice, with a visible uncertainty statement and correction control. A later transfer inquiry must use a different fictional situation and document which prompts and assistance were available. Do not derive a patron score or readiness judgment from any activity.

CORE SCREEN AND PAPER CARD
Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice with its unexplained “confirm your place” instruction. Offer route preference, availability unknown, none works and undecided choices. Permit a selected next action, an optional fictional response, or no action. Show concise descriptive feedback only when wanted. Keep revise, pause, stop, conceal and clear available as specified in sequence 15.

Example feedback: “Your draft selects asking what ‘confirm your place’ means if help is available. Help availability remains unknown. You may keep, change or leave this action undecided.” Feedback describes the draft; it does not certify that the action is feasible or that the patron understands it. Conceal this output with every other plan-bearing display.

OPTIONAL DELIBERATE PRACTICE
Offer one fictional change: “The notice still does not explain confirmation, and help availability is unknown.” Invite keeping, revising, leaving undecided or stopping. The practice focus is reconsidering a plan when a dependency is unresolved. Show no preferred route or praise for continuing. An optional selected response can identify what changed; explanation is never mandatory. Repetition is an invitation, not a prerequisite for assistance.

RETENTION AND TRANSFER INQUIRY — PROPOSED ONLY
If separately reviewed and voluntarily undertaken, use a later fictional activity without displaying the earlier plan. For example, an invented craft-session notice offers two times but gives contradictory confirmation instructions. Initially omit copied next-action examples, while keeping requested support available. Examine whether a reviewer identifies the uncertainty or chooses an acceptable response, including help-seeking or stopping. Record whether examples, explanation or assistance were supplied. This inquiry needs no personal records, contact details or stored patron history.

A later response could inform retention of the planning approach; adaptation to changed task features could inform transfer. Neither can be established by one completed exercise. An absent response supplies no evidence of inability. Reviewers must consider language demands, familiarity, prompting, fatigue and unavailable opportunities alongside any learning explanation. Appropriate delay, task comparability and acceptable review burden remain unknown.

NON-AI AND SERVICE ALTERNATIVES
Use the same card on paper or discuss the notice with available staff. Paper needs readable wording and discreet handling. Compare these approaches with clarifying the service notice itself; removing ambiguity may eliminate the need for practice. Retain objections to adding another learning task.

NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE
Prepare the paired screen outline and paper card, exact feedback examples, and a separate optional inquiry sheet identifying support conditions and rival explanations. Patron and librarian review must assess wording, access, privacy, workload and whether practice is wanted. Technical checks and human interaction testing remain pending before any pilot.
