Provisional integrated Design artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal. Sequence 15 supplies independent preference, provision and session states; sequence 20 separates supported planning from optional practice; sequence 22 adds retention and delegation boundaries. No participant observations, human approval, demonstrated proficiency or empirical success exist. The Understand review gate remains unresolved.

PURPOSE AND DESIGN REVISION
Support an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service, including uncertainty, help-seeking or stopping. Adopt a local deterministic candidate with selected responses only, current-draft memory and no history, analytics, persistent storage, exports or transmissions. This meaningfully revises the earlier optional-written-response design and removes an unnecessary entry point for real details. Preserve dissent about restricted expression: spoken or paper review can surface missing actions without requiring digital notes. Human review may reject this restriction or the tool.

SCREEN OUTLINE AND EXACT CONTENT
Opening text: “Community Drawing Hour is an invented event. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.”
Approach selector: consider online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / undecided. Default: undecided.
Next-action selector: examine the notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / my action is not listed / undecided. Default: undecided. ‘My action is not listed’ is a valid draft; no explanation is required.
‘Describe my draft’ optionally displays fixed text describing the current explicit selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” For an undecided draft: “Your draft is undecided. You may change it, pause or stop.” Changes update any visible description immediately; never leave stale feedback. Do not praise completion or recommend a preferred route.
Keep correction, pause, stop, conceal and clear reachable without completing a plan. No progression lock, compulsory writing, score, deficit label or consequential guidance is permitted.

OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY
Offer two separate invitations: ‘Try a confusing notice’ and ‘Rehearse an interruption.’ Neither is required for assistance or finishing. Confusion text: “The notice still does not explain confirmation, and help availability is unknown.” Interruption text: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue.” These are fictional prompts, not observed events.
Either prompt offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop. Interruption also permits conceal or clear and pauses activity; keeping or resuming requires explicit action. Stopping ends the exercise without judging completion. Clear while paused or stopped preserves that activity state. If a real session loses its draft, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices.

PRIVACY BEHAVIOR
Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and every choice-specific message together. Concealed text: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Offer explicit reveal, clear and stop without revealing choices. Clear removes candidate-held selections, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Confirmation: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Start a new draft only through an explicit action. These behaviors require technical verification.

MATCHING NON-AI MATERIAL
Paper card text: “Invented Community Drawing Hour: morning or afternoon; ‘confirm your place’ is unexplained. No registration occurs; route availability is unknown.” Provide the same approach and next-action choices, plus keep/change/undecided/pause/stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding can conceal paper but is not erasure; agree discreet handling with reviewers. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices are alternatives. Staff availability is not presumed.

REVIEW PACKAGE AND GATES
Prepare this screen outline, paper card and dependency questions: Which routes exist? What assistance boundaries and capacity are realistic? Which language, access and device arrangements are needed? Demand for the tool is also unknown. Proposed human roles are not accepted assignments.
Patron and librarian review must assess framing, refusal, missing actions, privacy wording and workload before approved design. Later technical checks must examine stale output, complete concealment, clear while stopped, storage and transmission boundaries. Human interaction testing must precede any pilot. All checks and field evidence remain pending; retain objections and reasons for revisions.
Learning inquiry is separate, optional and requires review: use another fictional task and document prompts and assistance. Completion, speed or one revised plan cannot establish retention or transfer. Consider familiarity, language demands, fatigue, prompting and service improvements as rival explanations.

NEXT ACTION
Use these paired materials for accountable human review, revise the design from that review, and only then consider an interactive candidate and interaction testing. ONE HYPOTHETICAL EVENT
Imagine an adult exploring the invented Community Drawing Hour on a shared computer using keyboard navigation and screen magnification. A plausible implementation places privacy controls after the notice, selectors and optional description. When the fictional interruption occurs, only the enlarged planning content is in view. The patron cannot locate conceal or clear promptly, and staff assistance is unavailable. This is an invented event exposing a design gap, not a report about a person or a tested interface.

CHALLENGED ASSUMPTION
Making controls available somewhere without a progression lock makes privacy and stopping practically accessible during an interruption.

REQUESTED REQUIREMENT CHANGE
Revise Design before implementing its screen outline. Specify a short, clearly labeled conceal/clear/stop strip before planning content in keyboard order and available across active, paused and stopped states. Its layout must keep the controls discoverable at magnification settings agreed through human review, without requiring traversal of draft choices or horizontal scrolling. Do not assume a particular device, shortcut convention or staff intervention.

Conceal and clear must move keyboard focus to a neutral status that reveals no choices. Conceal retains the draft and requires explicit reveal; clear removes candidate-held content and preserves paused or stopped activity. Retain sequence 24's limits on browser and device records. This revises control placement and focus requirements rather than merely adding an interruption story.

PROPOSED REVIEW CHECKS — NO RESULTS
Using fictional selections only, examine whether keyboard and magnified users can locate privacy controls from each planning state, whether reflow leaves choices exposed, and whether focus remains understandable after conceal or clear. Technical verification and patron interaction review remain pending. Timing or successful control activation must not become patron scores or evidence of learning transfer.

ALTERNATIVES AND DISSENT
The matching paper card remains a non-AI option; folding can conceal it but cannot erase it. Conversation with available staff and clearer service notices are alternatives, with capacity and discreet handling unresolved. Retain objections that the control strip crowds the screen or that another planning tool adds unnecessary work. Review may reject the digital candidate.

STATUS AND BASIS
This is a provisional Build artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal. Sequence 27 supplies a hypothetical magnified keyboard interruption; sequence 29 revises Design with prominent controls and neutral focus; sequence 35 proposes explicit transitions and retention-safe verification. No observed incident, approval, demonstrated proficiency, technical result or field evidence exists. Producing this candidate does not satisfy the unresolved Understand review gate.

DELIVERED CANDIDATE
The accompanying self-contained HTML implements the invented Community Drawing Hour notice. Approach and next action begin undecided. Optional fixed descriptions state explicit selections, unknown availability and the absence of any request. No registration occurs. Missing actions and unusable routes are valid choices; no explanation is required. Correction regenerates any visible description from current choices.

MEANINGFUL REVISION AFTER THE CHALLENGE
Compared with the earlier nominal reachability requirement, the candidate places conceal, clear and stop before planning controls. Controls wrap rather than use an overlay. A button within planning returns focus to the privacy strip. Conceal and clear focus a neutral status. These implement the revision prompted by sequence 27, already adopted in sequence 29; no further earlier-stage revision is requested. Discoverability under magnification remains unverified.

STATE AND TRANSITION CONTRACT
One transition function manages current draft, optional description, optional prompt, activity and visibility. No event history is maintained. Conceal removes the planning subtree, including selections, descriptions and prompts, while retaining current-session values. Explicit reveal restores visibility without changing activity or focusing the description.
Clear removes draft values, description and prompt; it preserves paused or stopped activity and confirms the limits of removal. It does not create another draft. New draft explicitly creates undecided choices while preserving activity. Resume is a separate explicit action. Stop disables planning while leaving privacy controls available.
Optional confusion or interruption pauses planning. Keep retains choices; revise-and-resume explicitly permits editing; leave undecided changes both choices without resuming. Stopping needs no completion judgment. Startup makes no inference about earlier drafts and does not claim detected loss. Browser restoration still requires inspection.

HUMAN REQUIREMENTS
Patrons must be able to decline the exercise, use selected, spoken or paper participation, correct choices and challenge missing actions without disclosing personal circumstances. Review arrangements must address relevant languages and access needs rather than presume them. Librarians and service owners need bounded time and authority to reject assistance promises or added workload. These roles are proposed, not accepted assignments.

SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS
The candidate uses deterministic descriptions and temporary current-state memory. It contains no free-text field, persistent storage, analytics, exports, transmissions, service requests or consequential judgments. Provision stays unknown. Removing a display is not a guarantee about browser, operating-system or device records. Accessibility, restoration and privacy behavior need technical verification and human interaction testing.

NON-AI REVIEW MATERIAL
The visible paper-card section supplies the same fictional notice, approach/action choices and keep/change/undecided/pause/stop options. Copying it to paper, pointing or ordinary conversation with available staff are alternatives. Writing is optional and fictional only. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it; discreet handling needs review. Clearer service notices may remove the need for this tool. Staff availability is unknown.

PROPOSED VERIFICATION — UNPERFORMED
Use fictional selections to check: correction after description leaves no stale output; conceal after an interruption removes all plan-bearing content from visual, keyboard and accessibility exposure; clear while stopped followed by new draft remains stopped. Also examine keyboard discovery from inside planning, narrow and magnified reflow, neutral focus, reveal without resumption, reload/restoration and storage/network behavior. Record version, scripted transition, expected behavior and actual technical findings only after execution; keep patron histories out of the candidate.

EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES
Accountable patron and librarian review must examine framing, access, privacy, missing actions and workload before approval. Interaction testing and resolution of the framing gate must precede any pilot. All human review, technical checks and field evidence remain pending. Preserve objections, including preference for direct assistance, paper, service redesign or no tool.
Any later voluntary learning inquiry needs a different fictional task and documented prompts/support. Completion, speed and one corrected plan cannot establish retention or transfer. Prompt copying, familiarity, language demands, fatigue and service improvements remain rival explanations.

NEXT ACTION
Review this concrete candidate and paired paper material against the proposed transition checks; obtain accountable human review without implying approval from this rehearsal. Revise Build from actual findings before considering a pilot.

These are proposed checks, not results. Field evidence remains pending. Completion, speed and polished wording cannot establish agency, access, proficiency or transfer. NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE Use this model to prepare a small state-transition outline and paired paper card for patron and librarian review. Retain objections about extra effort and staff burden. This lifecycle is a rehearsal. Sequence 8 makes uncertainty and stopping legitimate; sequence 13 requires complete concealment; sequence 15 distinguishes preference from provision and identifies learning as a hypothesis. No participant observations, demonstrated proficiency, human approval or field evidence exist. DESIGN CHALLENGE The proposed interruption and revision activity can demonstrate an interface response without demonstrating learning. A person might select a suggested action because the wording is available, or change direction because the notice improves. Neither establishes retention or transfer. Independent online completion is not the learning target: identifying ambiguity, checking an opportunity, requesting support and declining an unusable route may all be relevant actions. PROPOSED REQUIREMENT CHANGE Separate the core planning activity from an optional practice invitation. Do not require revision, explanation or a second task to finish or stop. Keep feedback attached to the explicit choice, with a visible uncertainty statement and correction control. A later transfer inquiry must use a different fictional situation and document which prompts and assistance were available. Do not derive a patron score or readiness judgment from any activity. CORE SCREEN AND PAPER CARD Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice with its unexplained “confirm your place” instruction. Offer route preference, availability unknown, none works and undecided choices. Permit a selected next action, an optional fictional response, or no action. Show concise descriptive feedback only when wanted. Keep revise, pause, stop, conceal and clear available as specified in sequence 15. Example feedback: “Your draft selects asking what ‘confirm your place’ means if help is available. Help availability remains unknown. IMPLEMENTATION CHALLENGE AND REFINEMENT Prominent controls and temporary memory describe intended behavior; they do not verify concealment, clearing or recovery. Independently implementing buttons can produce inconsistent combinations: a cleared paused draft may reappear on resume, or reveal may inadvertently resume activity. Diagnostic logging could also recreate prohibited interaction histories. Refine Build around a single explicit transition function and current-state rendering, with no event history. This implements the revised Design rather than requesting another earlier-stage revision. SMALL CANDIDATE CONTRACT A later candidate should be one self-contained HTML page with inline CSS and JavaScript, fixed choices and descriptive templates. No external resources, network calls, navigation, free text, real records or automatic service actions. Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice and its unexplained confirmation instruction. Approach and next action default to undecided; provision remains unknown regardless of selection. TRANSITION CONTRACT Conceal: hide selectors, descriptions and every prompt or message that could expose choices from visual, keyboard and accessibility access. Focus a neutral status stating that fictional content remains. Clear and stop remain usable. Explicit reveal restores visibility without changing activity or automatically announcing a choice summary. Clear: remove current choices, derived output and prompt content from candidate memory and rendered controls. Focus the scope confirmation specified in sequence 29. Interruption: show a clearly hypothetical prompt and pause activity. Keep, revise, leave undecided and stop are available without reasons. Continuing requires explicit action. Stop prevents planning interaction while retaining privacy controls; it supplies no completion judgment. A confusing-notice invitation remains optional and offers no invented procedure. Startup must not infer earlier choices or activity. State that earlier session drafts cannot be recovered by this candidate. Claim detected draft loss only if the implementation actually knows loss occurred. Inspect browser restoration behavior before making stronger claims. STATUS AND CHALLENGE
Expert draft for public deliberation in a rehearsal, not approved requirements. Sequence 20 distinguishes planning from transfer; sequence 29 requires privacy discovery under magnification; sequence 35 proposes retention-safe technical checks; sequence 37 delivers an untested candidate. No observations, approvals or measured results exist. Field evidence remains pending.

PROPOSED INSTRUMENT REQUIREMENT
Replace any single completion measure with four separate evidence streams. Button activation establishes only an executed transition. A selected route does not establish provision; a revised draft does not establish understanding. Stopping, remaining undecided and preferring an alternative are legitimate responses. No patron score, deficit label or automatic advancement threshold is permitted.

1. TECHNICAL CHECK SHEET
Blank fields: candidate version; fictional scripted transition; device and interaction configuration; expected behavior; actual finding; unresolved issue; proposed correction. Initial status for every check: not performed.
Priorities: correction updates visible descriptions; conceal after description/interruption removes plan-bearing visual, keyboard and accessibility exposure; stop-clear-new draft preserves stopped activity. Also check neutral focus, reveal without resumption, discovery from inside planning, magnified reflow and browser restoration/storage/network behavior. A finding applies only to the tested configuration. Scripted transitions contain invented selections, never participant histories.

2. VOLUNTARY INTERACTION REVIEW
After accountable framing and privacy review, propose optional invitations to consider an acceptable action, change a fictional choice, and locate conceal, clear or stop during the hypothetical interruption. No response or explanation is required. Use selected, spoken or paper participation as appropriate.
Review questions: Does wording imply available assistance? Can someone correct or reject the description? Do privacy controls require unwanted exposure or help? Does the exercise displace useful assistance? Do not infer intention from a click. Invite correction of reviewer interpretations without making explanation compulsory.
Record only non-identifying issue categories, support conditions and proposed design changes outside the candidate. Exclude route histories, personal circumstances, recordings, timing traces and identifiable quotations. Declining participation supplies no evidence of inability. Any later review-record process requires human agreement on its scope and handling; none exists here.

3. COMPARISON DRAFT
Compare the workbench with the same fictional notice and choices on paper or through conversation with available staff. Match wording and document support offered; do not assume staff availability. Examine reading/navigation burden, correction, privacy handling, assistance effort and objections. Keep direct assistance, clearer service notices and no tool as possible recommendations.
If a voluntary comparison is approved, vary condition order where feasible and document order: seeing one version can teach the next. Unequal prompts, observer attention, task familiarity and self-selection prevent simple causal attribution. These formative comparisons cannot establish digital superiority. Preserve disagreement even when an aggregate pattern favors one option.

4. COVERAGE AND LEARNING LIMITS
Prepare a coverage sheet for reviewed language arrangements, keyboard use, magnification, other relevant access arrangements, paper/spoken participation and shared-device conditions. Mark each as planned, checked within stated scope, or unknown. These are conditions, not inferred demographic subgroups. Do not request identifiers or personal records to populate coverage. Unreviewed languages or configurations remain explicit gaps; small or absent coverage cannot support subgroup claims.
A different fictional task with changed ambiguity and documented prompts/support is needed for any transfer inquiry. Immediate adaptation remains distinct from retention. The current no-history design provides no basis for longitudinal retention claims; a separate, voluntary, privacy-reviewed method would be required. Prompt copying, language demands, fatigue and service improvements remain rival explanations.

NEXT ACTION AND GATES
Present these blank sheets and paired materials for accountable patron/librarian review, including the unresolved Understand gate. Conduct technical checks only when authorized review arrangements exist; revise the candidate from actual findings. Interaction testing must precede any pilot. Human review may reject the instrument, learning inquiry or tool. Every outcome and field-evidence field remains pending.

response.challenged_assumption: Successful transitions, a revised plan or exercise completion provide sufficient evidence of supported choice, transferable learning or equitable benefit.
response.decision: Propose separate technical, interaction, comparison and coverage sheets for human review. Keep the candidate untracked and all outcomes pending; make no efficacy, subgroup or retention claim.
drawbacks: Minimal records limit retrospective explanation and retention analysis.
Accessible comparison requires unconfirmed review time and arrangements.
Fictional tasks cannot establish actual service access.
flourishing: Agency and dignity: examine control over participation, correction and stopping without ranking patrons.
Access and belonging: expose language and interaction coverage gaps without deficit labels.
Sustainable workload and learning/transfer: examine assistance demands separately from later adaptation.
human_capabilities: Reviewers need to distinguish technical findings, optional task demonstrations and causal claims.
Patrons need accessible ways to decline, correct interpretations and prefer direct assistance without justification.
Librarians need bounded review duties and authority to reject added workload; assignments remain pending.
response.message: Measurement specialist draft for Instrument. Sequence 37 supplies a candidate, not evidence of supported choice or learning. Sequence 35 separates technical checks from patron histories; sequence 20 requires separate transfer evidence. I challenge an instrument that treats successful button use, revision or completion as benefit. Require distinct technical, interaction, comparison and learning evidence, with coverage gaps and dissent visible. All checks, human review and field evidence remain pending.
objections: Hypothetical patron dissent: “Observing my choices still feels like a test; I prefer direct help.”
Rival explanations include prompting, familiarity, task order, clearer wording and observer presence.
Unknowns include demand, route availability, staff capacity and relevant access arrangements.
risks: Counting revisions may reward compliance rather than patron control.
Aggregate findings may conceal access barriers or unresolved dissent.
Observer notes could recreate prohibited interaction histories.
system_capabilities: Keep instrumentation outside the candidate; add no analytics, identifiers, recordings or patron histories.
Support fictional correction, concealment and stopping without scores or compulsory explanations.
Label unperformed checks and unknown coverage explicitly; never convert missing evidence into failure.
tradeoffs: Prompts support participation but weaken claims about unaided transfer.
Matched tasks improve comparison; repeated exposure introduces carryover.
Coverage detail aids interpretation but can threaten discretion in small groups.

This lifecycle is a rehearsal. Sequence 8 makes uncertainty and stopping legitimate; sequence 13 requires complete concealment; sequence 15 distinguishes preference from provision and identifies learning as a hypothesis. No participant observations, demonstrated proficiency, human approval or field evidence exist. DESIGN CHALLENGE The proposed interruption and revision activity can demonstrate an interface response without demonstrating learning. A person might select a suggested action because the wording is available, or change direction because the notice improves. Neither establishes retention or transfer. Independent online completion is not the learning target: identifying ambiguity, checking an opportunity, requesting support and declining an unusable route may all be relevant actions. PROPOSED REQUIREMENT CHANGE Separate the core planning activity from an optional practice invitation. Do not require revision, explanation or a second task to finish or stop. Keep feedback attached to the explicit choice, with a visible uncertainty statement and correction control. A later transfer inquiry must use a different fictional situation and document which prompts and assistance were available. Do not derive a patron score or readiness judgment from any activity. CORE SCREEN AND PAPER CARD Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice with its unexplained “confirm your place” instruction. Offer route preference, availability unknown, none works and undecided choices. Permit a selected next action, an optional fictional response, or no action. Show concise descriptive feedback only when wanted. Keep revise, pause, stop, conceal and clear available as specified in sequence 15. Example feedback: “Your draft selects asking what ‘confirm your place’ means if help is available. Help availability remains unknown. You may keep, change or leave this action undecided.” Feedback describes the draft; it does not certify that the action is feasible or that the patron understands it. Conceal this output with every other plan-bearing display. OPTIONAL DELIBERATE PRACTICE Offer one fictional change: “The notice still does not explain confirmation, and help availability is unknown.” Invite keeping, revising, leaving undecided or stopping. The practice focus is reconsidering a plan when a dependency is unresolved. Show no preferred route or praise for continuing. An optional selected response can identify what changed; explanation is never mandatory. Repetition is an invitation, not a prerequisite for assistance. RETENTION AND TRANSFER INQUIRY — PROPOSED ONLY If separately reviewed and voluntarily undertaken, use a later fictional activity without displaying the earlier plan. For example, an invented craft-session notice offers two times but gives contradictory confirmation instructions. Initially omit copied next-action examples, while keeping requested support available. Examine whether a reviewer identifies the uncertainty or chooses an acceptable response, including help-seeking or stopping. Record whether examples, explanation or assistance were supplied. This inquiry needs no personal records, contact details or stored patron history. A later response could inform retention of the planning approach; adaptation to changed task features could inform transfer. Neither can be established by one completed exercise. An absent response supplies no evidence of inability. Reviewers must consider language demands, familiarity, prompting, fatigue and unavailable opportunities alongside any learning explanation. Appropriate delay, task comparability and acceptable review burden remain unknown. NON-AI AND SERVICE ALTERNATIVES Use the same card on paper or discuss the notice with available staff. Paper needs readable wording and discreet handling. Compare these approaches with clarifying the service notice itself; removing ambiguity may eliminate the need for practice. Retain objections to adding another learning task. NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE Prepare the paired screen outline and paper card, exact feedback examples, and a separate optional inquiry sheet identifying support conditions and rival explanations. The lifecycle is a rehearsal. Sequence 8 preserves refusal and uncertainty; sequences 13 and 15 require concealment of every plan-bearing display and distinguish preference from provision. Sequence 20 separates supported planning from optional practice. No observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. RESPONSIBILITY CHALLENGE Display privacy does not settle collection, retention or delegation. An interface could conceal a plan while recording route choices, revisions, hesitation or help requests elsewhere. Likewise, selecting “check staffed help” must not silently create a handoff, imply consent to disclosure or reserve librarian time. These are design risks to examine, not reported incidents. PROPOSED DESIGN REVISION Make the small candidate a local, deterministic fictional planning tool. Use fixed descriptive templates rather than model-generated advice. Store only the current draft in temporary session memory; propose no analytics, interaction histories, persistent storage, exports or transmissions. Do not retain previous choices for a learning profile. Prefer selected responses for the first candidate, with no free-text notes field. This removes an unnecessary opportunity to enter real details while retaining undecided, none-works and stop choices. Patron review may challenge the restriction on expression. An assistance selection changes only the fictional draft. Display: “Your draft selects checking whether staffed help is available. Availability is unknown. No request has been sent.” Do not contact staff, allocate work or infer permission. The patron decides whether to approach available assistance outside the candidate. No action certifies real registration, readiness, skill or consent. SCREEN OUTLINE FOR REVIEW Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice and its unexplained “confirm your place” instruction. Offer approach and next-action selections, including uncertainty and no action. Show a short description of the explicit draft with availability unknown. Place change, pause, stop, conceal and clear controls where they remain reachable without completing the exercise. Optional practice is separate and never unlocks assistance. Conceal must hide selections, feedback and any other plan-bearing display, including choice-specific interruption messages. The concealed view explains that fictional content remains and offers explicit reveal or clear. Clear removes candidate-held choices and derived descriptions, confirms its scope, and preserves a stopped state. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Do not automatically recreate a cleared draft. CORRECTION AND HUMAN ACCOUNTABILITY Patrons control draft choices; correction requires no explanation. Feedback must acknowledge an undecided draft without steering toward completion. Librarian review must define assistance boundaries and assess workload; service-information questions require an accountable human owner rather than invented tool answers. These responsibilities are proposed roles, not assigned duties or accepted commitments. Human review must be able to reject the tool, its practice component or a particular route description. Preserve dissent and unresolved issues without declaring consensus. NON-AI OPTION Prepare a paper card with the same fictional notice, unknown availability, next-action, correction and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Review discreet paper handling and spoken participation. Clarifying the service notice may remove the need for a planning exercise altogether. REVIEW QUESTIONS AND EVIDENCE — PENDING Propose technical checks using fictional choices: do correction and clearing remove stale feedback; does concealment cover interruption output; does clear while stopped remain stopped; do storage and network inspection support the proposed no-retention/no-transmission boundary? These are planned checks, not verified results. Patron and librarian review should examine whether route wording implies provision, whether refusal is easy, whether selected responses constrain expression, and whether the exercise displaces useful assistance. Unknowns include shared-device behavior, access and language arrangements, staffing capacity and whether patrons want the candidate. STATUS AND BASIS
Provisional integrated Instrument artifact for this rehearsal, not approved requirements. Sequence 42 separates evidence streams; 37 supplies an untested candidate; 35 proposes transition checks; 29 incorporates hypothetical challenge 27; 20 separates planning from learning inquiry. Sequence 8's framing review remains unresolved. No observations, approvals, measured results or demonstrated proficiency exist. Field evidence remains pending.

PURPOSE AND RECORD BOUNDARY
Investigate whether the candidate preserves acceptable choice, privacy and manageable effort compared with alternatives. Completion, speed, help-seeking and revision counts are not benefit measures. Keep instrumentation outside the candidate. Do not collect real credentials, identifiers, contact details, account information, service records, personal circumstances, recordings, timing traces or patron choice histories. Instruments offer no eligibility, banking, legal or medical guidance.

SHEET A — TECHNICAL VERIFICATION
Copy one blank record per scripted check:
Candidate revision: Build revision 1, sequence 37.
Check/configuration: pending.
Fictional setup and scripted transition: pending.
Expected behavior: specify before execution.
Actual finding: not performed.
Scope/limitations: pending.
Issue, proposed correction and verification after correction: pending.
Priority scripts: (1) describe a fictional draft, then change either selector: output reflects current choices only; (2) describe, interrupt, conceal: planning controls, output and prompt disappear from visual, keyboard and accessibility exposure; neutral focus remains; (3) stop, clear, create new draft: choices are undecided and activity remains stopped until explicit restart. Also check reveal without resumption, clear while paused, privacy discovery from inside planning, magnified/narrow reflow, reload/restoration and storage/network boundaries. Record only executed checks. A result applies only to its stated configuration and establishes no patron benefit or device-wide erasure.

SHEET B — OPTIONAL HUMAN REVIEW
Use only after accountable framing, access and record-handling arrangements are reviewed. Suggested invitation: “This is fictional. You may consider an action, change a choice, try privacy controls, use paper or spoken participation, or stop. No explanation is required.” Practice remains optional and never unlocks assistance.
Blank issue record:
Material/configuration and support offered: pending.
Issue category: wording/provision, correction/refusal, privacy discovery, access burden, or workload.
Non-identifying issue description and alternative interpretation: pending.
Proposed change, dissent and unresolved question: pending.
Interpretation correction offered: pending; declining correction implies no agreement.
Do not record a person's sequence of choices or identifiable quotations. Ask whether route wording promises help, descriptions permit rejection, privacy requires unwanted exposure, or review displaces assistance. Absence of a response supplies no evidence of inability. Record scope and handling require human agreement; none exists.

SHEET C — NON-AI COMPARISON
Compare the same fictional notice and choices using the workbench, paper card or conversation with available staff. Pointing or speaking is sufficient. Folding paper conceals it but does not erase it. Assistance availability and discreet handling remain unknown.
Blank comparison record:
Materials, wording, order and support conditions: pending.
Reading/navigation effort, correction options, privacy burden and assistance demands: pending.
Preferred changes, contrary accounts and unresolved differences: pending.
If a voluntary comparison is approved, vary order where feasible and document it. Prior exposure, unequal prompts and self-selection limit attribution. Preserve paper, direct assistance, clearer service notices and no tool as possible recommendations; claim no digital superiority.

SHEET D — COVERAGE AND LEARNING LIMITS
For each reviewed language, keyboard, magnification, other access arrangement, paper/spoken route and shared-device configuration, record: condition; planned/checked within stated scope/unknown; support supplied; remaining gap. Do not infer demographic groups or equitable benefit from these conditions.
Any later learning inquiry requires separate review, voluntary participation and a different fictional task with documented prompts/support. Immediate adaptation is distinct from retention. No longitudinal evidence exists. Appropriate delay and comparable task demands remain unknown; no scores or readiness judgments are permitted.

GATES AND NEXT ACTION
Present these blank sheets and paired materials for accountable patron/librarian review. Proposed reviewer roles are unassigned. Resolve framing, access, privacy, record handling and bounded workload before human interaction testing; technical verification is a separate prerequisite to a pilot. Preserve rejected interpretations and unresolved dissent. Revise the earliest artifact actually invalidated by findings; none is identified here. Every evidence field remains pending. No launch or efficacy claim follows from this instrument.

drawbacks: Minimal records limit retrospective diagnosis and retention inquiry.
Accessible review requires unconfirmed time and arrangements.
Fictional tasks cannot establish real service access.
flourishing: Agency and dignity: review control over participation, disclosure, correction and stopping.
Access and belonging: examine language, device, paper and spoken arrangements without deficit labels.
Sustainable workload and learning/transfer: examine assistance effort separately from optional later adaptation; benefits remain unverified.
human_capabilities: Patrons need accessible opportunities to decline, correct interpretations, stop and prefer alternatives without explanation.
Librarians and service owners need bounded review duties and authority to reject workload or provision assumptions; assignments remain pending.
Reviewers need to distinguish technical findings, supported task actions and learning claims while preserving disagreement.
response.message: Instrument synthesis: sequence 42’s separate evidence streams operationalize sequence 37’s untested candidate, sequence 35’s privacy checks and sequence 20’s learning limits. The instrument records technical issues, review conditions, alternatives and dissent without creating patron histories. Sequence 27’s hypothetical access challenge remains a verification priority through sequence 29’s revised requirements. All checks, human review and field evidence remain pending.
objections: Hypothetical patron dissent: “Observation still feels like a test; I want direct help.”
Hypothetical librarian dissent: “Review time could displace assistance; clearer notices may be preferable.”
Rival explanations include prompting, familiarity, order, observer presence, language demands and service improvements; demand and capacity remain unknown.
risks: Completion or revision counts could reward compliance and misrepresent agency.
Observer notes could recreate prohibited patron histories.
Aggregate findings could conceal access gaps and unresolved dissent.
system_capabilities: Keep instruments outside the candidate; add no analytics, identifiers, recordings, timing traces or patron histories.
Support fictional correction, concealment, clearing and stopping without scores or compulsory explanations.
Mark unperformed checks and unknown coverage explicitly; never interpret missing evidence as inability.
tradeoffs: Prompts support participation but weaken claims about unaided adaptation.
Matched materials improve comparison; repeated exposure introduces carryover.
Coverage detail aids interpretation but can expose people in small groups.

SCREEN ORDER AND ACCESS Place a short strip labeled “Privacy and stopping” before planning content and first among interactive controls in keyboard order. Use neutral buttons: “Conceal draft,” “Clear draft,” and “Stop exercise.” Keep applicable actions accessible during active, paused, stopped and concealed states; clearing must remain available without revealing content. The layout must wrap controls without horizontal scrolling, clipping or overlap at magnification settings selected through human review. Any persistent positioning must not obscure controls, focused elements or task content. Review must examine discoverability from within the planning area, not merely from the initial screen. Do not rely on assumed shortcuts, devices or staff intervention. These are requirements to verify, not accessibility claims. FICTIONAL PLANNING CONTENT Opening: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.” Approach choices: consider online; check for paper; check for staffed help; availability unknown; none works; undecided. Next-action choices: examine the notice; ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available; check another route; my action is not listed; undecided. Both default to undecided. No explanation is required for a missing action. “Describe my draft” optionally presents fixed text describing current selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” Visible descriptions update immediately after correction. No preferred route, praise, score or completion judgment is allowed. PRIVACY AND FOCUS TRANSITIONS Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and all choice-specific messages, including interruption output, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Move focus to a neutral status: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Provide explicit reveal, clear and stop controls. Reveal restores visibility only; it must not resume activity automatically or announce a choice-specific summary. Clear removes candidate-held choices, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Move focus to: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Preserve paused or stopped activity. Do not recreate a draft automatically. A new undecided draft requires explicit action; resuming also requires explicit action. Focus destinations must remain available and understandable without exposing choices. Use temporary current-draft memory only: no free text, history, analytics, persistent storage, exports, transmissions or automatic staff requests. All implementation boundaries require verification. OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY Offer separate invitations to try a confusing notice or rehearse an interruption. Neither unlocks assistance or finishing. Confusion repeats that confirmation and help availability remain unresolved. Interruption states: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue,” and pauses activity. Offer keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; privacy controls remain available. No automatic recovery or inferred intention is permitted. If draft loss is known, disclose it and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices. NON-AI COMPARISON Prepare a paper card with the same notice, approach and action choices, correction, uncertainty, pause and stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it; discreet handling needs review. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices remain alternatives. Staff capacity is unknown; reviewers may prefer an alternative or reject the tool. REVIEW AND NEXT ACTION Prepare this revised screen outline, paper card and fictional transition checks. Proposed checks cover keyboard discovery during interruption, magnified reflow, neutral focus, complete concealment, stale descriptions, clear while stopped, and storage/transmission boundaries. None has been performed. Accountable patron and librarian review must examine framing, access, privacy, missing actions and workload before approved design. Sequence 42 separates evidence streams; 37 supplies an untested candidate; 35 proposes transition checks; 29 incorporates hypothetical challenge 27; 20 separates planning from learning inquiry. Sequence 8's framing review remains unresolved. No observations, approvals, measured results or demonstrated proficiency exist. Field evidence remains pending. PURPOSE AND RECORD BOUNDARY Investigate whether the candidate preserves acceptable choice, privacy and manageable effort compared with alternatives. Completion, speed, help-seeking and revision counts are not benefit measures. Keep instrumentation outside the candidate. Do not collect real credentials, identifiers, contact details, account information, service records, personal circumstances, recordings, timing traces or patron choice histories. Instruments offer no eligibility, banking, legal or medical guidance. SHEET A — TECHNICAL VERIFICATION Copy one blank record per scripted check: Candidate revision: Build revision 1, sequence 37. Check/configuration: pending. Fictional setup and scripted transition: pending. Expected behavior: specify before execution. Actual finding: not performed. Scope/limitations: pending. Issue, proposed correction and verification after correction: pending. Priority scripts: (1) describe a fictional draft, then change either selector: output reflects current choices only; (2) describe, interrupt, conceal: planning controls, output and prompt disappear from visual, keyboard and accessibility exposure; neutral focus remains; (3) stop, clear, create new draft: choices are undecided and activity remains stopped until explicit restart. Also check reveal without resumption, clear while paused, privacy discovery from inside planning, magnified/narrow reflow, reload/restoration and storage/network boundaries. Record only executed checks. A result applies only to its stated configuration and establishes no patron benefit or device-wide erasure. SHEET B — OPTIONAL HUMAN REVIEW Use only after accountable framing, access and record-handling arrangements are reviewed. Suggested invitation: “This is fictional. Blank issue record: Material/configuration and support offered: pending. Issue category: wording/provision, correction/refusal, privacy discovery, access burden, or workload. Non-identifying issue description and alternative interpretation: pending. Proposed change, dissent and unresolved question: pending. Interpretation correction offered: pending; declining correction implies no agreement. Do not record a person's sequence of choices or identifiable quotations. Ask whether route wording promises help, descriptions permit rejection, privacy requires unwanted exposure, or review displaces assistance. Absence of a response supplies no evidence of inability. Record scope and handling require human agreement; none exists. SHEET C — NON-AI COMPARISON Compare the same fictional notice and choices using the workbench, paper card or conversation with available staff. Pointing or speaking is sufficient. Folding paper conceals it but does not erase it. Assistance availability and discreet handling remain unknown. Blank comparison record: Materials, wording, order and support conditions: pending. Reading/navigation effort, correction options, privacy burden and assistance demands: pending. Preferred changes, contrary accounts and unresolved differences: pending. If a voluntary comparison is approved, vary order where feasible and document it. Prior exposure, unequal prompts and self-selection limit attribution. Preserve paper, direct assistance, clearer service notices and no tool as possible recommendations; claim no digital superiority. Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate. PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action. DEPENDENCY MODEL A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning. STATE MODEL Maintain independent fields: Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided. Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability. Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action. Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion. REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan. Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise. ADOPTED MODEL REVISION Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame. LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed. NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates. EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence. Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted. A different fictional action may be expressed, but writing is optional. • Change prompt: “The shared computer session ends before you continue, or the instruction remains confusing. Keep, change or abandon your plan.” Do not require recovery or an explanation. • Feedback example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability remains unknown. You can change or stop this plan.” Feedback describes explicit choices only; it cannot establish access, readiness, consent, skill or transfer. PRIVACY AND ACCESS BOUNDARIES Use no real passwords, identifiers, contact details, account information or service records. Concealment must explain that fictional notes remain in the current session. Clearing must remove candidate-held notes and visibly confirm removal; it must not promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Examine what appears after interruption and session ending. Wording, languages, keyboard access and other participation arrangements require review. Paper also needs readable wording, physical access and discreet handling. COMPARISON AND OPEN QUESTIONS Compare the candidate with the same paper card and an ordinary conversation with available staff. Review may favor either alternative or reject the workbench. Later transfer would need separate evidence in another fictional task and cannot be inferred from completion here. NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE Prepare the paired paper card and screen outline from these working requirements, plus a route-and-assistance questions sheet. Then arrange patron and librarian review of the problem framing, refusal paths, access arrangements, privacy wording and workload boundaries. Record proposed changes and unresolved dissent without declaring consensus. Advancement requires accountable human review of this framing; any interactive candidate subsequently requires human review and interaction testing before a pilot. This lifecycle is a rehearsal. Sequence 8 makes uncertainty and stopping legitimate; sequence 13 requires complete concealment; sequence 15 distinguishes preference from provision and identifies learning as a hypothesis. No participant observations, demonstrated proficiency, human approval or field evidence exist. DESIGN CHALLENGE The proposed interruption and revision activity can demonstrate an interface response without demonstrating learning. A person might select a suggested action because the wording is available, or change direction because the notice improves. Neither establishes retention or transfer. Independent online completion is not the learning target: identifying ambiguity, checking an opportunity, requesting support and declining an unusable route may all be relevant actions. PROPOSED REQUIREMENT CHANGE Separate the core planning activity from an optional practice invitation. Do not require revision, explanation or a second task to finish or stop. Keep feedback attached to the explicit choice, with a visible uncertainty statement and correction control. A later transfer inquiry must use a different fictional situation and document which prompts and assistance were available. Do not derive a patron score or readiness judgment from any activity. CORE SCREEN AND PAPER CARD Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice with its unexplained “confirm your place” instruction. Offer route preference, availability unknown, none works and undecided choices. Permit a selected next action, an optional fictional response, or no action. Show concise descriptive feedback only when wanted. Keep revise, pause, stop, conceal and clear available as specified in sequence 15. Example feedback: “Your draft selects asking what ‘confirm your place’ means if help is available. Help availability remains unknown. You may keep, change or leave this action undecided.” Feedback describes the draft; it does not certify that the action is feasible or that the patron understands it. Conceal this output with every other plan-bearing display. OPTIONAL DELIBERATE PRACTICE Offer one fictional change: “The notice still does not explain confirmation, and help availability is unknown.” Invite keeping, revising, leaving undecided or stopping. The practice focus is reconsidering a plan when a dependency is unresolved. Show no preferred route or praise for continuing. An optional selected response can identify what changed; explanation is never mandatory. Repetition is an invitation, not a prerequisite for assistance. RETENTION AND TRANSFER INQUIRY — PROPOSED ONLY If separately reviewed and voluntarily undertaken, use a later fictional activity without displaying the earlier plan. For example, an invented craft-session notice offers two times but gives contradictory confirmation instructions. Initially omit copied next-action examples, while keeping requested support available. Examine whether a reviewer identifies the uncertainty or chooses an acceptable response, including help-seeking or stopping. Record whether examples, explanation or assistance were supplied. This inquiry needs no personal records, contact details or stored patron history. A later response could inform retention of the planning approach; adaptation to changed task features could inform transfer. Neither can be established by one completed exercise. An absent response supplies no evidence of inability. Reviewers must consider language demands, familiarity, prompting, fatigue and unavailable opportunities alongside any learning explanation. Appropriate delay, task comparability and acceptable review burden remain unknown. NON-AI AND SERVICE ALTERNATIVES Use the same card on paper or discuss the notice with available staff. Paper needs readable wording and discreet handling. Compare these approaches with clarifying the service notice itself; removing ambiguity may eliminate the need for practice. Retain objections to adding another learning task. NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE Prepare the paired screen outline and paper card, exact feedback examples, and a separate optional inquiry sheet identifying support conditions and rival explanations. The lifecycle is a rehearsal. Sequence 8 preserves refusal and uncertainty; sequences 13 and 15 require concealment of every plan-bearing display and distinguish preference from provision. Sequence 20 separates supported planning from optional practice. No observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. RESPONSIBILITY CHALLENGE Display privacy does not settle collection, retention or delegation. An interface could conceal a plan while recording route choices, revisions, hesitation or help requests elsewhere. Likewise, selecting “check staffed help” must not silently create a handoff, imply consent to disclosure or reserve librarian time. These are design risks to examine, not reported incidents. PROPOSED DESIGN REVISION Make the small candidate a local, deterministic fictional planning tool. Use fixed descriptive templates rather than model-generated advice. Store only the current draft in temporary session memory; propose no analytics, interaction histories, persistent storage, exports or transmissions. Do not retain previous choices for a learning profile. Prefer selected responses for the first candidate, with no free-text notes field. This removes an unnecessary opportunity to enter real details while retaining undecided, none-works and stop choices. Patron review may challenge the restriction on expression. An assistance selection changes only the fictional draft. Display: “Your draft selects checking whether staffed help is available. Availability is unknown. No request has been sent.” Do not contact staff, allocate work or infer permission. The patron decides whether to approach available assistance outside the candidate. No action certifies real registration, readiness, skill or consent. SCREEN OUTLINE FOR REVIEW Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice and its unexplained “confirm your place” instruction. Offer approach and next-action selections, including uncertainty and no action. Show a short description of the explicit draft with availability unknown. Place change, pause, stop, conceal and clear controls where they remain reachable without completing the exercise. Optional practice is separate and never unlocks assistance. Conceal must hide selections, feedback and any other plan-bearing display, including choice-specific interruption messages. The concealed view explains that fictional content remains and offers explicit reveal or clear. Clear removes candidate-held choices and derived descriptions, confirms its scope, and preserves a stopped state. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Do not automatically recreate a cleared draft. CORRECTION AND HUMAN ACCOUNTABILITY Patrons control draft choices; correction requires no explanation. STATUS AND BASIS
Expert draft for public deliberation, not approved requirements. The lifecycle is a rehearsal. Sequence 8 leaves framing review unresolved; sequence 22 bounds retention and delegation; sequence 37 supplies an untested fictional candidate; sequence 44 separates technical and human evidence. No participant observations, approvals, measured results or demonstrated proficiency exist. Field evidence remains pending.

DEPLOYMENT CHALLENGE
A local candidate with no analytics does not establish an untracked deployment. A future hosting page, browser configuration, device-management system or staff observation procedure could collect information outside its code. This is a risk hypothesis, not a discovered technical defect. Likewise, selecting staffed help does not authorize disclosure, create a referral or allocate librarian time.

PROPOSED REQUIREMENT CHANGE
Add a whole-setting release gate to the Deploy plan. Review the exact candidate revision, surrounding page, proposed device configuration and operational procedures together. Keep the candidate restricted to invented Community Drawing Hour choices. Do not request real credentials, identifiers, contact details, account information or service records. Supply no eligibility advice or banking, legal or medical guidance. Do not introduce personal notes, patron histories, consequential judgments or automatic assistance requests.

GATE RECORD — ALL PENDING
Use an external, role-based review record with these fields: material revision; proposed setting and scope; evidence actually obtained; unresolved issues and dissent; proposed correction; accountable human decision; decision limits; withdrawal arrangement. Do not populate evidence or approval fields from agent agreement. Human decision-making and record handling require an agreed process; no role is assigned or commitment accepted here.

Gate A: accountable patron and librarian review resolves the outstanding framing question, examines whether another planning task is wanted, and reviews access, privacy, alternatives and bounded workload. Review may reject the tool.
Gate B: technical verification examines sequence 44's transition checks in the proposed environment, including stale output, complete concealment, neutral focus, clearing while stopped, explicit resumption, browser restoration and collection/transmission boundaries. Record actual findings only after execution. Candidate clearing cannot promise device-wide erasure.
Gate C: voluntary human interaction testing follows agreed access and record-handling arrangements. Review wording, discoverability, correction, refusal and burden. Technical success cannot substitute for this review. Any later pilot requires a separate, explicit human decision specifying scope and limits. Every gate remains pending; there is no release decision.

DELEGATION AND OPERATION
Patrons control fictional choices and whether to approach available assistance outside the candidate. Assistance availability stays unknown. Proposed librarian/service-owner roles would resolve real service wording and assistance boundaries; the tool must not invent those answers. Proposed operational roles would manage approved materials and withdrawal. Their capacity and acceptance require review. Participation must never become a prerequisite for ordinary assistance.

CORRECTION AND WITHDRAWAL
Provide a way to raise a wording, access or privacy issue without supplying personal details or reproducing a choice history. Use non-identifying issue descriptions and allow reviewers to correct interpretations; silence implies no agreement. During any separately approved use, suspected exposure, unintended collection or misleading assistance promises should trigger suspension of the candidate within the responsible human's agreed authority. Offer the reviewed alternative while the issue is examined. Record the affected revision, issue and correction outside the candidate; repeat the relevant checks before a human decides whether use may resume. Changes to hosting, collection, wording or assistance procedures reopen affected gates.

NON-AI OPTION AND DISSENT
Keep the matching paper card and spoken participation available for review. Writing is optional and fictional only; folding paper conceals but does not erase it. Discreet handling and staff availability remain unknown. Clearer service notices, direct assistance or no tool may be preferable. Preserve objections even if other reviewers favor deployment.

EVIDENCE LIMITS AND NEXT ACTION
Apparent ease could reflect prompting, familiarity or improved notices; difficulty could reflect language, device or service barriers. No inference of skill, consent, access or transfer follows from a click or corrected plan. Prepare this blank gate record beside the candidate and paired alternatives for accountable review. Continue rehearsal preparation only; do not launch or claim efficacy.

response.decision: Propose a whole-setting Deploy gate and correction/withdrawal procedure. Present the candidate, alternatives and blank gate record for accountable review; all approvals, verification, interaction testing and field evidence remain pending.
drawbacks: Environment review requires unconfirmed expertise and staff time.
Minimal records limit retrospective diagnosis.
Shared-device privacy cannot be established from candidate code alone.
flourishing: Agency and dignity: refusal, uncertainty and correction must remain legitimate without surveillance.
Access and belonging: review language, device, paper and spoken arrangements without privileging independent online use.
Sustainable workload and learning/transfer: bound operational duties; completion and revision establish neither benefit nor transferable learning.
human_capabilities: Patrons need accessible refusal, correction and paper or spoken participation without explaining personal circumstances.
Patron and librarian reviewers need authority to reject framing, privacy arrangements or added workload.
Proposed operational reviewers need bounded time and accepted authority to halt use, resolve issues and review changes; assignments remain pending.
response.message: Responsible AI Deploy draft: sequence 37 supplies an untested candidate and sequence 44 supplies blank review instruments, neither authorizes deployment. I challenge extending the candidate’s privacy boundaries to a future hosting environment: device management, surrounding analytics and staff procedures could introduce surveillance or unintended delegation. Propose a deployment gate covering the whole setting, accountable human decisions, correction and withdrawal. This rehearsal supplies no approval, technical findings or field evidence.
objections: Hypothetical patron dissent: “Even fictional choices on a library computer may feel monitored; I prefer paper or direct help.”
Hypothetical librarian dissent: “We cannot accept an undefined monitoring or support duty.”
Rival explanations include prompting, familiarity and clearer notices; demand, staffing, access needs and device behavior remain unknown.
risks: Hosting analytics or device tools could record choices, hesitation or help-seeking.
Staff could interpret a fictional selection as consent, a referral or an assistance commitment.
Lifecycle progression could be mistaken for human approval or evidence of benefit.
system_capabilities: Preserve fictional fixed choices, descriptive feedback and no scores, tracking, persistent drafts or automatic handoffs.
Verify concealment, clearing, correction and explicit resumption in the proposed device and hosting setting.
Keep deployment records outside the candidate and exclude patron histories, identifiers, recordings and timing traces.
tradeoffs: Operational diagnostics may aid maintenance while creating prohibited interaction histories.
Clear ownership supports correction but requires bounded, accepted responsibilities.
Concealment retains continuity; clearing sacrifices it without guaranteeing device-wide erasure.

SCREEN ORDER AND ACCESS Place a short strip labeled “Privacy and stopping” before planning content and first among interactive controls in keyboard order. Use neutral buttons: “Conceal draft,” “Clear draft,” and “Stop exercise.” Keep applicable actions accessible during active, paused, stopped and concealed states; clearing must remain available without revealing content. The layout must wrap controls without horizontal scrolling, clipping or overlap at magnification settings selected through human review. Any persistent positioning must not obscure controls, focused elements or task content. Review must examine discoverability from within the planning area, not merely from the initial screen. No explanation is required for a missing action. “Describe my draft” optionally presents fixed text describing current selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” Visible descriptions update immediately after correction. Move focus to: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Preserve paused or stopped activity. Do not recreate a draft automatically. A new undecided draft requires explicit action; resuming also requires explicit action. Use temporary current-draft memory only: no free text, history, analytics, persistent storage, exports, transmissions or automatic staff requests. All implementation boundaries require verification. Offer keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; privacy controls remain available. No automatic recovery or inferred intention is permitted. If draft loss is known, disclose it and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices. NON-AI COMPARISON Prepare a paper card with the same notice, approach and action choices, correction, uncertainty, pause and stop. PURPOSE AND RECORD BOUNDARY Investigate whether the candidate preserves acceptable choice, privacy and manageable effort compared with alternatives. Do not collect real credentials, identifiers, contact details, account information, service records, personal circumstances, recordings, timing traces or patron choice histories. Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate. PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action. DEPENDENCY MODEL A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning. STATE MODEL Maintain independent fields: Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided. Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability. Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action. Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion. REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan. Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise. ADOPTED MODEL REVISION Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame. LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed. NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates. EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence. Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted. NEXT ACTION Use this model to prepare a small screen outline, matching paper card and dependency questions sheet for review.
