PROBLEM FRAME Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping. ADOPTED REVISION The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. These are working requirements awaiting human review, not approved commitments. FICTIONAL REVIEW MATERIAL Exercise text: “Imagine a made-up library event called Community Drawing Hour. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.” Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline: • Approach: online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / pause or stop. • Next action: examine the fictional notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / leave undecided / stop. A different fictional action may be expressed, but writing is optional. • Change prompt: “The shared computer session ends before you continue, or the instruction remains confusing. Keep, change or abandon your plan.” Do not require recovery or an explanation. • Feedback example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability remains unknown. You can change or stop this plan.” Feedback describes explicit choices only; it cannot establish access, readiness, consent, skill or transfer. PRIVACY AND ACCESS BOUNDARIES Use no real passwords, identifiers, contact details, account information or service records. Concealment must explain that fictional notes remain in the current session. Clearing must remove candidate-held notes and visibly confirm removal; it must not promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Examine what appears after interruption and session ending. Wording, languages, keyboard access and other participation arrangements require review. Paper also needs readable wording, physical access and discreet handling. COMPARISON AND OPEN QUESTIONS Compare the candidate with the same paper card and an ordinary conversation with available staff. Review may favor either alternative or reject the workbench. Unknowns include actual route availability, assistance boundaries, staff capacity, language needs, shared-device behavior and whether another planning task is wanted. Preserve objections even if other reviewers favor the candidate. EVIDENCE PLAN — ALL PENDING Proposed review questions: Can reviewers identify an acceptable action, including no action? Do route labels imply unavailable provision? Can they revise, conceal, clear and stop with understandable consequences? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens does each approach introduce? Use fictional content only and retain contrary accounts. Difficulty could reflect instructions or unavailable opportunities; apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity. Later transfer would need separate evidence in another fictional task and cannot be inferred from completion here. NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE Prepare the paired paper card and screen outline from these working requirements, plus a route-and-assistance questions sheet. Then arrange patron and librarian review of the problem framing, refusal paths, access arrangements, privacy wording and workload boundaries. Record proposed changes and unresolved dissent without declaring consensus. Advancement requires accountable human review of this framing; any interactive candidate subsequently requires human review and interaction testing before a pilot. DESIGN CHALLENGE The proposed interruption and revision activity can demonstrate an interface response without demonstrating learning. A person might select a suggested action because the wording is available, or change direction because the notice improves. Neither establishes retention or transfer. Independent online completion is not the learning target: identifying ambiguity, checking an opportunity, requesting support and declining an unusable route may all be relevant actions. PROPOSED REQUIREMENT CHANGE Separate the core planning activity from an optional practice invitation. Do not require revision, explanation or a second task to finish or stop. Keep feedback attached to the explicit choice, with a visible uncertainty statement and correction control. A later transfer inquiry must use a different fictional situation and document which prompts and assistance were available. Do not derive a patron score or readiness judgment from any activity. CORE SCREEN AND PAPER CARD Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice with its unexplained “confirm your place” instruction. Offer route preference, availability unknown, none works and undecided choices. Permit a selected next action, an optional fictional response, or no action. Show concise descriptive feedback only when wanted. Keep revise, pause, stop, conceal and clear available as specified in sequence 15. Example feedback: “Your draft selects asking what ‘confirm your place’ means if help is available. Help availability remains unknown. You may keep, change or leave this action undecided.” Feedback describes the draft; it does not certify that the action is feasible or that the patron understands it. Conceal this output with every other plan-bearing display. OPTIONAL DELIBERATE PRACTICE Offer one fictional change: “The notice still does not explain confirmation, and help availability is unknown.” Invite keeping, revising, leaving undecided or stopping. The practice focus is reconsidering a plan when a dependency is unresolved. Show no preferred route or praise for continuing. An optional selected response can identify what changed; explanation is never mandatory. Repetition is an invitation, not a prerequisite for assistance. RETENTION AND TRANSFER INQUIRY — PROPOSED ONLY If separately reviewed and voluntarily undertaken, use a later fictional activity without displaying the earlier plan. For example, an invented craft-session notice offers two times but gives contradictory confirmation instructions. Initially omit copied next-action examples, while keeping requested support available. Examine whether a reviewer identifies the uncertainty or chooses an acceptable response, including help-seeking or stopping. Record whether examples, explanation or assistance were supplied. This inquiry needs no personal records, contact details or stored patron history. A later response could inform retention of the planning approach; adaptation to changed task features could inform transfer. Neither can be established by one completed exercise. An absent response supplies no evidence of inability. Reviewers must consider language demands, familiarity, prompting, fatigue and unavailable opportunities alongside any learning explanation. Appropriate delay, task comparability and acceptable review burden remain unknown. NON-AI AND SERVICE ALTERNATIVES Use the same card on paper or discuss the notice with available staff. Paper needs readable wording and discreet handling. Compare these approaches with clarifying the service notice itself; removing ambiguity may eliminate the need for practice. Retain objections to adding another learning task. NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE Prepare the paired screen outline and paper card, exact feedback examples, and a separate optional inquiry sheet identifying support conditions and rival explanations. STATUS AND BASIS
Provisional integrated Deploy artifact for public deliberation. Sequence 37 supplies an untested Build candidate; 44 supplies blank evidence instruments; 49 proposes whole-setting review and withdrawal. Sequence 8’s framing gate remains unresolved. Sequence 20 separates supported planning from optional practice and learning inquiry. No participant observations, approvals, technical findings, measured outcomes or demonstrated proficiency exist. Field evidence remains pending.

STAGE DECISION
Adopt whole-setting review as a provisional Deploy requirement. Prepare a readiness dossier rather than release the candidate. The concern in sequence 49 is a risk hypothesis, not a discovered defect. No earlier artifact is invalidated by supplied findings, so no earlier-stage revision is requested. Missing approval remains a gate, not evidence that framing has failed.

REVIEW DOSSIER
Identify Build revision 1, sequence 37, and pair it with its fictional paper/spoken card and sequence 44’s blank sheets. Add the proposed surrounding page, device/session configuration, assistance procedure and issue-handling arrangement; all setting details remain unspecified. Review scope is the invented Community Drawing Hour only. No real registration or assistance request occurs. Keep demand, route provision and staff availability unknown until accountable review supplies evidence.

GATE RECORD — BLANK
Material revision and proposed setting: pending.
Gate and evidence needed: specify before review.
Evidence actually obtained and its scope: pending.
Unresolved issue, dissent and alternative interpretation: pending.
Proposed correction and checks after correction: pending.
Accountable human role, decision and limits: unassigned/pending.
Withdrawal arrangement and capacity: pending.
Agent agreement cannot populate approval or evidence fields. Record handling requires human agreement; preserve non-identifying issues rather than individual choice histories.

HUMAN GATES — ALL PENDING
A. Framing and arrangements: accountable patron and librarian review must examine whether the activity is wanted, refusal, access and language arrangements, privacy, alternatives, record handling and bounded workload. Service owners must be able to challenge route wording. Proposed roles are not accepted assignments. Review may reject the tool or prefer service redesign.
B. Interaction review: after agreed arrangements and technical checks appropriate to the proposed setting, voluntary fictional interaction testing must examine correction, stopping, privacy discovery and burden. Selected, spoken and paper participation receive equal standing. No explanation or practice task is required; ordinary assistance must not depend on participation. Silence or refusal establishes neither agreement nor inability.
C. Pilot decision: only a separate explicit human decision may permit a bounded pilot after unresolved prerequisites are addressed. Its record must specify revision, setting, scope, access arrangements, accepted responsibilities, stopping conditions and remaining uncertainty. No such decision exists.

SYSTEM VERIFICATION GATE — UNPERFORMED
Use sequence 44’s technical sheet with fictional scripted selections. Check correction without stale descriptions; conceal after description and interruption across visual, keyboard and accessibility exposure; neutral focus; stopped-clear-new-draft without automatic restart; reveal without resumption. Examine magnified/narrow reflow, discovery from within planning, browser restoration, storage and transmission in the surrounding setting. Candidate code intentions alone cannot establish these properties. Each actual finding would apply only to its stated configuration and would establish neither benefit nor device-wide erasure.

OPERATION AND CORRECTION — PROPOSED
Keep choices fictional, descriptions deterministic and provision unknown. No credentials, identifiers, contact details, account information, service records, personal notes, consequential scores or eligibility, banking, legal or medical guidance. Add no analytics, patron histories or automatic handoffs. Issue reporting must permit non-identifying descriptions and correction of interpretations.
For any separately approved use, an accountable human with accepted authority should suspend the affected candidate when suspected exposure, collection, inaccessible controls or misleading provision appears. Offer a reviewed alternative, document the issue outside the candidate, correct it and repeat affected checks before deciding whether use resumes. Changes to hosting, device configuration, wording or assistance procedures reopen affected gates.

ALTERNATIVES AND EVIDENCE LIMITS
Compare the same fictional notice on paper or through conversation with available staff. Writing is optional; folding conceals paper but does not erase it. Discreet handling and staff capacity remain unknown. Clearer service notices or no tool may be preferable. Preserve dissent rather than infer consensus. Prompting, familiarity, language demands, fatigue, task order and service improvements are rival explanations. Completion and revision cannot establish access, retention or transfer; later learning inquiry requires separate review and another fictional task with documented support.

NEXT ACTION
Present this dossier and blank gate record for accountable review, then obtain actual technical findings and voluntary interaction evidence under agreed arrangements. Keep every gate pending until evidence and human decisions exist. This rehearsal authorizes no launch and establishes no efficacy.

Check correction without stale descriptions; conceal after description and interruption across visual, keyboard and accessibility exposure; neutral focus; stopped-clear-new-draft without automatic restart; reveal without resumption. Examine magnified/narrow reflow, discovery from within planning, browser restoration, storage and transmission in the surrounding setting. Candidate code intentions alone cannot establish these properties. Each actual finding would apply only to its stated configuration and would establish neither benefit nor device-wide erasure.

OPERATION AND CORRECTION — PROPOSED
Keep choices fictional, descriptions deterministic and provision unknown. No credentials, identifiers, contact details, account information, service records, personal notes, consequential scores or eligibility, banking, legal or medical guidance. Add no analytics, patron histories or automatic handoffs. Issue reporting must permit non-identifying descriptions and correction of interpretations.
For any separately approved use, an accountable human with accepted authority should suspend the affected candidate when suspected exposure, collection, inaccessible controls or misleading provision appears. Offer a reviewed alternative, document the issue outside the candidate, correct it and repeat affected checks before deciding whether use resumes. Changes to hosting, device configuration, wording or assistance procedures reopen affected gates.

ALTERNATIVES AND EVIDENCE LIMITS
Compare the same fictional notice on paper or through conversation with available staff. Writing is optional; folding conceals paper but does not erase it. Discreet handling and staff capacity remain unknown. Clearer service notices or no tool may be preferable. Preserve dissent rather than infer consensus. Prompting, familiarity, language demands, fatigue, task order and service improvements are rival explanations. Completion and revision cannot establish access, retention or transfer; later learning inquiry requires separate review and another fictional task with documented support.

NEXT ACTION
Present this dossier and blank gate record for accountable review, then obtain actual technical findings and voluntary interaction evidence under agreed arrangements. Keep every gate pending until evidence and human decisions exist. This rehearsal authorizes no launch and establishes no efficacy.

PROBLEM FRAME Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping. ADOPTED REVISION The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.” Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline: • Approach: online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / pause or stop. • Next action: examine the fictional notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / leave undecided / stop. IMPLEMENTATION CHALLENGE AND REFINEMENT Prominent controls and temporary memory describe intended behavior; they do not verify concealment, clearing or recovery. Independently implementing buttons can produce inconsistent combinations: a cleared paused draft may reappear on resume, or reveal may inadvertently resume activity. Diagnostic logging could also recreate prohibited interaction histories. Refine Build around a single explicit transition function and current-state rendering, with no event history. This implements the revised Design rather than requesting another earlier-stage revision. SMALL CANDIDATE CONTRACT A later candidate should be one self-contained HTML page with inline CSS and JavaScript, fixed choices and descriptive templates. No external resources, network calls, navigation, free text, real records or automatic service actions. Present the invented Community Drawing Hour notice and its unexplained confirmation instruction. Approach and next action default to undecided; provision remains unknown regardless of selection. Optional description must update immediately when visible choices change and must state that no request was sent and no understanding, skill or access was established. Keep only current draft values, description visibility, optional prompt, activity and concealment state in temporary memory. Derive output from those values rather than retaining previous descriptions. Do not serialize choices into storage, URLs, exports, logs or hidden page fields. These are proposed implementation boundaries requiring inspection, not guarantees about browser or device records. TRANSITION CONTRACT Conceal: hide selectors, descriptions and every prompt or message that could expose choices from visual, keyboard and accessibility access. Focus a neutral status stating that fictional content remains. Clear and stop remain usable. Explicit reveal restores visibility without changing activity or automatically announcing a choice summary. Clear: remove current choices, derived output and prompt content from candidate memory and rendered controls. Focus the scope confirmation specified in sequence 29. Interruption: show a clearly hypothetical prompt and pause activity. Keep, revise, leave undecided and stop are available without reasons. Continuing requires explicit action. Stop prevents planning interaction while retaining privacy controls; it supplies no completion judgment. A confusing-notice invitation remains optional and offers no invented procedure. Startup must not infer earlier choices or activity. State that earlier session drafts cannot be recovered by this candidate. Claim detected draft loss only if the implementation actually knows loss occurred. Inspect browser restoration behavior before making stronger claims. Use wrapping layout and visible focus indicators; avoid fixed overlays that obscure magnified content. Provide a neutral way from the planning area to focus the privacy strip without requiring a shortcut or staff intervention. Discoverability, reflow and assistive-technology behavior require human-selected conditions and testing; control placement alone establishes none of them. Record candidate version, scripted transition, expected behavior and any actual technical finding only after execution. Keep choices, timing, hesitation and participant interaction histories out of the candidate. Separate technical findings from later voluntary human review; neither becomes a patron score. Also inspect reload/restoration, narrow or magnified layout, and absence of storage or transmission. All checks are unperformed. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it; discreet handling needs review. Conversation with available staff and clearer service notices remain alternatives; availability and workload are unknown. STATUS AND BASIS
Expert draft for public deliberation, not approved requirements. This lifecycle is a rehearsal. Sequence 37 supplies an untested fictional candidate; 42 separates evidence streams; 44 supplies blank sheets; 51 holds release behind whole-setting and human gates. No participant observations, approvals, technical findings, measured outcomes or demonstrated proficiency exist. Field evidence remains pending.

MEASUREMENT CHALLENGE
Separate evidence streams are necessary but do not specify what each can justify. Non-identifying issue sheets support formative correction; they cannot establish issue prevalence, individual improvement, equitable benefit or causal effects. Do not expand collection merely to obtain a stronger claim. Evaluate the available evidence against a bounded claim, rather than treating lifecycle completion or fewer reported issues as success.

PROPOSED CLAIM LEDGER — ALL FINDINGS PENDING
For each claim record: exact claim; revision and setting; evidence needed; evidence actually obtained; contrary evidence and rival explanation; coverage limits; permissible conclusion; proposed action and accountable human decision.

Technical behavior: use sequence 44's fictional scripts for correction, concealment, focus, explicit resumption and stopped-clear-new-draft behavior, plus restoration and collection boundaries in sequence 51's proposed setting. Status: not performed. A passing check would support only the executed behavior in that configuration, not usability, device-wide erasure or benefit.

Supported choice: separately reviewed voluntary interaction material could identify whether wording permits refusal, correction, uncertainty, help-seeking and privacy control, and what burdens arise. Status: no accounts obtained. Choosing an offered action, finishing or stopping alone establishes none of these outcomes. Declining review establishes neither inability nor acceptance.

Comparison: examine the same invented Community Drawing Hour notice through the workbench, a paper card and conversation with available staff. Status: not conducted; assistance availability unknown. Document material wording, condition order and support arrangements without preserving individual choice histories. Compare reading/navigation effort, correction, privacy handling and assistance demands. Preserve clearer notices, direct help and no tool as possible recommendations. Formative accounts cannot establish digital superiority or an average treatment effect.

Coverage: mark each proposed language, keyboard, magnification, other access arrangement, paper/spoken route and shared-device condition as planned, checked within stated scope or unknown. Status: relevant coverage and all checks pending. Conditions do not identify demographic subgroups. With no reviewed subgroup evidence, no subgroup benefit or equity claim is available. Small-condition descriptions must not expose a person; omit sensitive detail and retain the gap. Absence of complaints is especially inconclusive where participation is inaccessible.

Learning and transfer: immediate revision under the same prompts is task adaptation, not demonstrated transfer. A separately reviewed inquiry would need a different fictional task with changed surface features, comparable demands and documented support. Retention additionally requires an agreed delay and a feasible voluntary method compatible with privacy boundaries. Status: no method approved and no evidence obtained. The current issue-only records cannot establish individual change over time; retain that claim as unknown rather than introduce tracking.

CAUSAL THREATS AND DISSENT
Seeing one condition can teach the next; unequal prompting, familiarity, observer attention, fatigue, language demands and self-selection can explain apparent differences. Service clarification can improve planning independently of the workbench. Document these limitations at the arrangement level and avoid causal attribution. Preserve objections even if other accounts favor the candidate. Do not turn silence, withdrawal or an unavailable route into a patron deficit.

PROPOSED DECISION RULES
Missing findings mean unevaluated, not passed or failed. Actual privacy or access findings would support correction and affected rechecks within an accountable human process. Favorable technical findings would permit only their scoped technical conclusion; they cannot replace framing review, interaction evidence or a separate pilot decision. Review may recommend paper, available direct assistance, service redesign or no tool. No automatic threshold, score or agent agreement authorizes use.

NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATES
Present this ledger beside sequence 44's blank sheets and sequence 51's dossier for accountable review. Resolve framing, access, record handling and bounded workload arrangements; obtain actual technical findings and voluntary interaction evidence under agreed conditions. Proposed roles remain unassigned. Keep launch, efficacy, equitable benefit and transfer claims pending. No earlier artifact is invalidated by supplied findings, so no earlier-stage revision is requested.

response.challenged_assumption: Privacy-bounded issue sheets and separate evidence streams are sufficient to establish efficacy, subgroup benefit or transfer without claim-specific evidence and decision limits.
response.decision: Propose a bounded evaluation claim ledger and explicit inference limits. Keep all outcomes pending; seek accountable review and actual scoped evidence before any pilot decision or benefit claim.
drawbacks: Issue records cannot establish prevalence, individual change or causal effects.
Fictional planning cannot establish actual service access.
Comparison and accessible review require unconfirmed capacity.
flourishing: Agency and dignity: examine rejection, correction, concealment and stopping without interpreting compliance as benefit.
Access and belonging: preserve paper, spoken and supported participation while exposing language and device coverage gaps.
Sustainable workload and learning/transfer: examine assistance burden separately from adaptation and retention; all benefits remain unknown.
human_capabilities: Reviewers need to distinguish supplied artifacts, executed checks, voluntary accounts and causal claims.
Patrons need accessible refusal, correction and alternative participation without justification.
Librarians and accountable reviewers need bounded duties and authority to reject the tool or suspend proposed use; assignments remain pending.
response.message: Measurement Evaluate draft: sequence 51 supplies a readiness dossier, while sequence 44 supplies blank instruments and sequence 37 an untested candidate. None supplies evaluative findings. I challenge treating issue sheets as sufficient for efficacy, subgroup or transfer claims: their privacy boundaries deliberately exclude evidence needed for those inferences. Propose a claim-by-claim evidence ledger and bounded decision rules. Human gates, technical checks and field evidence remain pending.
objections: Hypothetical patron dissent: “A voluntary observation can still feel like a test; I prefer direct help.”
Rival explanations include prompting, familiarity, condition order, observer attention, language demands and clearer service wording.
Unknowns include demand, route availability, staff capacity, relevant review coverage and feasible transfer arrangements.
risks: Few recorded issues could be mistaken for acceptability despite inaccessible review or nonparticipation.
Aggregated impressions could conceal missing access conditions and dissent.
Pressure for outcome metrics could recreate prohibited patron histories.
system_capabilities: Keep evaluation outside the candidate without identifiers, personal records, recordings, timing traces or patron histories.
Associate actual technical findings with candidate revision, configuration and scripted fictional transition.
Label absent evidence and unreviewed conditions explicitly; supply no patron scores or automatic release decisions.
tradeoffs: Minimal collection protects discretion but limits longitudinal inference.
Matched wording improves comparison; repeated exposure introduces carryover.
Support enables participation but complicates claims about unaided transfer.

Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate. PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action. DEPENDENCY MODEL A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning. STATE MODEL Maintain independent fields: Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided. Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability. Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action. Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion. REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan. Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise. ADOPTED MODEL REVISION Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame. LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed. NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates. EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence. Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted. NEXT ACTION Use this model to prepare a small screen outline, matching paper card and dependency questions sheet for review. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping. ADOPTED REVISION The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. IMPLEMENTATION CHALLENGE AND REFINEMENT Prominent controls and temporary memory describe intended behavior; they do not verify concealment, clearing or recovery. Independently implementing buttons can produce inconsistent combinations: a cleared paused draft may reappear on resume, or reveal may inadvertently resume activity. Diagnostic logging could also recreate prohibited interaction histories. Refine Build around a single explicit transition function and current-state rendering, with no event history. This implements the revised Design rather than requesting another earlier-stage revision. STATUS AND DECISION
This is a provisional integrated Evaluate artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal. Sequence 44 supplies blank instruments; 51 supplies whole-setting release gates; 57 specifies permissible claim limits. The candidate and review materials exist as supplied project data. No executed checks, participant observations, approvals, measured outcomes or demonstrated proficiency exist. Field evidence remains pending. Adopt the following evaluation framework as a review draft, not approved requirements. Keep deployment and any pilot pending.

EVIDENCE INVENTORY
Available: fictional candidate, paired paper/spoken material, proposed transition scripts, blank issue sheets and readiness dossier. These establish preparation only. Technical findings: not performed. Human accounts and comparisons: not obtained. Access coverage, workload feasibility, retention and transfer: unknown. Missing evidence means unevaluated, rather than passed or failed. The meaningful privacy-placement revision following the hypothetical challenge remains a requirement to verify, not evidence of successful protection.

REUSABLE CLAIM RECORD
Claim and permissible conclusion: specify before inquiry.
Candidate revision, setting and material: pending.
Evidence required and collection boundary: pending review.
Evidence actually obtained, source type and scope: pending.
Contrary account, dissent and rival explanation: pending.
Coverage gap and uncertainty: pending.
Proposed correction or alternative: pending.
Accountable human decision, accepted responsibility and limits: unassigned/pending.
Use non-identifying issue records outside the candidate. Do not fill findings or approval fields from agent agreement. Record handling requires human agreement. Silence and refusal establish neither acceptance nor inability.

CLAIMS AND INFERENCE LIMITS
Technical behavior: use sequence 44's fictional scripts to examine correction, complete concealment, neutral focus, reveal without resumption and stop-clear-new-draft behavior. Include reflow, restoration and collection boundaries in sequence 51's exact proposed setting. An executed check could support only that behavior in its stated configuration; it would not establish usability, device-wide erasure or benefit. All findings are pending.
Supported choice: separately reviewed voluntary interaction could identify wording, correction, refusal, privacy-discovery and participation burdens. A selection, completed draft, revision or stopping action alone cannot establish agency or understanding. Invite correction of interpretations without requiring an explanation. No accounts exist.
Alternatives and access: compare the same fictional notice through the workbench, paper and conversation with available staff. Document wording, order and support arrangements without retaining individual histories. Examine reading/navigation effort, discretion, correction and assistance demands. Mark language, keyboard, magnification, other access and shared-device conditions as planned, checked within scope or unknown. Unreviewed conditions remain gaps; do not infer subgroup or equitable benefit. Comparison and coverage are pending.
Learning: immediate revision with the same prompts cannot establish transfer. A separately reviewed inquiry would require a different fictional task with comparable demands and documented support. Retention additionally needs an agreed delay and a feasible voluntary method. Current issue records cannot establish individual change over time. Keep these claims unknown rather than expand tracking.

DELIBERATION AND REQUIREMENTS
Preserve dissent even where favorable accounts later arise. Apparent improvement could reflect prompting, familiarity, condition order, observer attention, fatigue or clearer service wording. Difficulty could reflect language, device or service barriers. Formative accounts cannot establish digital superiority or causal effects.
Human requirements: accessible voluntary review, authority to reject interpretations or the tool, bounded accepted duties and ordinary assistance independent of participation. System requirements: fictional fixed choices, descriptive correction, privacy controls and no personal-data entry, tracking, patron scores or automatic handoffs. Neither set is human-approved.
Paper or spoken planning is a non-AI option; writing is optional. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it. Staff availability and discreet handling remain unknown. Clearer service notices, direct assistance or no tool remain legitimate recommendations.

NEXT ACTION AND GATES
Present this ledger with sequence 44's sheets and sequence 51's dossier for accountable framing, access, privacy, record-handling and workload review. Obtain scoped technical findings and voluntary interaction evidence under agreed arrangements before any separate pilot decision. Actual findings should trigger correction and affected rechecks, or review of the earliest artifact they invalidate. No supplied finding presently warrants an earlier-stage revision. This rehearsal establishes neither launch authorization nor efficacy.

response.decision: Adopt the provisional evaluation ledger and inference limits. Next, review it alongside the instruments and whole-setting dossier, resolve human gates and obtain actual scoped evidence. Hold deployment, any pilot and benefit claims pending; request no earlier-stage revision without an invalidating finding.
drawbacks: Issue-only records cannot establish prevalence, individual improvement or causal effects.
Fictional planning cannot establish actual service access.
Accessible review and comparison require unconfirmed staff time and arrangements.
flourishing: Agency and dignity: refusal, uncertainty, help-seeking and correction must receive neutral treatment.
Access and belonging: examine language, device, paper and spoken arrangements without privileging independent online completion.
Sustainable workload and learning/transfer: examine assistance burden separately from adaptation, retention and transfer; benefits remain unknown.
human_capabilities: Patrons need accessible refusal, correction, concealment, stopping and paper or spoken participation without justification.
Librarians and service owners need bounded duties and authority to reject workload, provision claims or the candidate.
Accountable reviewers need to distinguish technical findings, voluntary accounts and learning claims; roles and acceptance remain pending.
response.message: Evaluate synthesis: sequence 57’s claim limits extend sequence 44’s blank instruments and sequence 51’s whole-setting gates. The supplied artifacts support review preparation, but contain no evaluative findings. Adopt a bounded claim ledger that preserves dissent, alternatives and uncertainty. Human review, technical verification, interaction testing and field evidence remain pending. No supplied finding invalidates an earlier artifact, so no earlier-stage revision is requested.
objections: Hypothetical patron dissent: “Even voluntary observation feels like a test; I prefer direct assistance.”
Hypothetical librarian dissent: “Review could displace assistance; clearer service notices may be preferable.”
Rivals include prompting, familiarity, order, fatigue and clearer wording; demand, routes, staffing and relevant access arrangements remain unknown.
risks: Few complaints could be mistaken for acceptability when review is inaccessible.
Favorable technical findings could overshadow dissent or missing access conditions.
Pressure for stronger outcome claims could recreate prohibited patron histories.
system_capabilities: Preserve fictional choices, correctable descriptions and independent activity/privacy states without sensitive-data entry, scores or automatic handoffs.
Keep evaluation outside the candidate, excluding identifiers, service records, recordings, timing traces and patron choice histories.
Associate actual findings with revision and configuration; expose missing evidence and coverage without automatic release decisions.
tradeoffs: Minimal collection protects discretion while limiting longitudinal inference.
Matched materials improve comparison, but repeated exposure can teach the next condition.
Support enables participation while complicating claims about unaided transfer.

REVISION AND SCOPE Revise Design once: replace nominal reachability with explicit placement, reflow and focus requirements. The dependency model and problem frame remain applicable; the earliest artifact needing this change is Design. The unresolved Understand human-review gate remains pending, without requesting another revision of Understand. SCREEN ORDER AND ACCESS Place a short strip labeled “Privacy and stopping” before planning content and first among interactive controls in keyboard order. Use neutral buttons: “Conceal draft,” “Clear draft,” and “Stop exercise.” Keep applicable actions accessible during active, paused, stopped and concealed states; clearing must remain available without revealing content. The layout must wrap controls without horizontal scrolling, clipping or overlap at magnification settings selected through human review. Any persistent positioning must not obscure controls, focused elements or task content. Review must examine discoverability from within the planning area, not merely from the initial screen. Do not rely on assumed shortcuts, devices or staff intervention. These are requirements to verify, not accessibility claims. FICTIONAL PLANNING CONTENT Opening: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.” Approach choices: consider online; check for paper; check for staffed help; availability unknown; none works; undecided. Next-action choices: examine the notice; ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available; check another route; my action is not listed; undecided. Both default to undecided. No explanation is required for a missing action. “Describe my draft” optionally presents fixed text describing current selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” Visible descriptions update immediately after correction. No preferred route, praise, score or completion judgment is allowed. PRIVACY AND FOCUS TRANSITIONS Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and all choice-specific messages, including interruption output, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Move focus to a neutral status: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Provide explicit reveal, clear and stop controls. Reveal restores visibility only; it must not resume activity automatically or announce a choice-specific summary. Clear removes candidate-held choices, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Move focus to: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Preserve paused or stopped activity. Do not recreate a draft automatically. A new undecided draft requires explicit action; resuming also requires explicit action. Focus destinations must remain available and understandable without exposing choices. Use temporary current-draft memory only: no free text, history, analytics, persistent storage, exports, transmissions or automatic staff requests. All implementation boundaries require verification. OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY Offer separate invitations to try a confusing notice or rehearse an interruption. Neither unlocks assistance or finishing. Confusion repeats that confirmation and help availability remain unresolved. Interruption states: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue,” and pauses activity. Offer keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; privacy controls remain available. No automatic recovery or inferred intention is permitted. If draft loss is known, disclose it and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices. NON-AI COMPARISON Prepare a paper card with the same notice, approach and action choices, correction, uncertainty, pause and stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it; discreet handling needs review. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices remain alternatives. Staff capacity is unknown; reviewers may prefer an alternative or reject the tool. REVIEW AND NEXT ACTION Prepare this revised screen outline, paper card and fictional transition checks. Proposed checks cover keyboard discovery during interruption, magnified reflow, neutral focus, complete concealment, stale descriptions, clear while stopped, and storage/transmission boundaries. None has been performed. Accountable patron and librarian review must examine framing, access, privacy, missing actions and workload before approved design. Technical verification and human interaction testing must precede any pilot. Field evidence remains pending. Preserve contrary accounts and reasons for changes. Separate any voluntary learning inquiry using another fictional task and documented support conditions; completion, speed or one revised plan cannot establish retention or transfer.","prototype_html":"","title":"Revised Design synthesis: discoverable privacy controls and supported choice"},"content_hash":"3f234e938602b268ec8f69c3c64e17b5fad30fe53fda30a65729cd72ee6aa306","id":"design","parent_revision":1,"revision":2,"trigger_seq":29},"evaluate":{"content":{"body":"STATUS AND DECISION This is a provisional integrated Evaluate artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal. A selection, completed draft, revision or stopping action alone cannot establish agency or understanding. Invite correction of interpretations without requiring an explanation. No accounts exist. Document wording, order and support arrangements without retaining individual histories. Examine reading/navigation effort, discretion, correction and assistance demands. Formative accounts cannot establish digital superiority or causal effects. Human requirements: accessible voluntary review, authority to reject interpretations or the tool, bounded accepted duties and ordinary assistance independent of participation. System requirements: fictional fixed choices, descriptive correction, privacy controls and no personal-data entry, tracking, patron scores or automatic handoffs. Neither set is human-approved. GATES AND NEXT ACTION Present these blank sheets and paired materials for accountable patron/librarian review. Proposed reviewer roles are unassigned. Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate. PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action. DEPENDENCY MODEL A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning. STATE MODEL Maintain independent fields: Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided. Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability. Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action. Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion. REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan. Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise. ADOPTED MODEL REVISION Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame. LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed. NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates. EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence. Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted. NEXT ACTION Use this model to prepare a small screen outline, matching paper card and dependency questions sheet for review. Sequence 4 identifies route reality, privacy and assistance capacity as unresolved. Sequence 6 challenges the assumption that three offered routes constitute meaningful choice. The seed supplies the fictional task and restrictions. No participant observations, human approvals or field results exist. PROBLEM FRAME Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping. ADOPTED REVISION The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. These are working requirements awaiting human review, not approved commitments. FICTIONAL REVIEW MATERIAL Exercise text: “Imagine a made-up library event called Community Drawing Hour. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.” Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline: • Approach: online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / pause or stop. • Next action: examine the fictional notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / leave undecided / stop. A different fictional action may be expressed, but writing is optional. • Change prompt: “The shared computer session ends before you continue, or the instruction remains confusing. Keep, change or abandon your plan.” Do not require recovery or an explanation. • Feedback example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability remains unknown. You can change or stop this plan.” Feedback describes explicit choices only; it cannot establish access, readiness, consent, skill or transfer. PRIVACY AND ACCESS BOUNDARIES Use no real passwords, identifiers, contact details, account information or service records. Concealment must explain that fictional notes remain in the current session. Clearing must remove candidate-held notes and visibly confirm removal; it must not promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Examine what appears after interruption and session ending. Wording, languages, keyboard access and other participation arrangements require review. Paper also needs readable wording, physical access and discreet handling. COMPARISON AND OPEN QUESTIONS Compare the candidate with the same paper card and an ordinary conversation with available staff. Review may favor either alternative or reject the workbench. Unknowns include actual route availability, assistance boundaries, staff capacity, language needs, shared-device behavior and whether another planning task is wanted. Preserve objections even if other reviewers favor the candidate. EVIDENCE PLAN — ALL PENDING Proposed review questions: Can reviewers identify an acceptable action, including no action? Do route labels imply unavailable provision? Can they revise, conceal, clear and stop with understandable consequences? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens does each approach introduce? Use fictional content only and retain contrary accounts. Difficulty could reflect instructions or unavailable opportunities; apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity. Later transfer would need separate evidence in another fictional task and cannot be inferred from completion here. NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE Prepare the paired paper card and screen outline from these working requirements, plus a route-and-assistance questions sheet. Then arrange patron and librarian review of the problem framing, refusal paths, access arrangements, privacy wording and workload boundaries. Record proposed changes and unresolved dissent without declaring consensus. Advancement requires accountable human review of this framing; any interactive candidate subsequently requires human review and interaction testing before a pilot. STATUS AND BASIS
Expert scenario draft for public deliberation in a rehearsal, not an approved requirement. Sequence 44 supplies an optional review invitation and blank instruments. Sequence 51 requires ordinary assistance independent of participation. Sequence 59 preserves voluntary review and bounded duties but supplies no executed evidence. No participant observations, approvals or field findings exist.

ONE HYPOTHETICAL OBJECTION
Imagine a proposed comparison session for the invented Community Drawing Hour. The only available librarian would provide ordinary assistance and invite the fictional review. An imagined patron objects: “You are also the person I need help from; saying no may not feel safe.” The invitation states that participation is optional, yet the arrangement leaves the patron uncertain about whether refusing will affect assistance. This is one invented objection, not testimony or a finding about actual library practice.

CHALLENGED ASSUMPTION
A voluntary invitation and a stated independence rule are sufficient to protect refusal when the reviewer also controls access to ordinary assistance.

REQUESTED REQUIREMENT CHANGE
Revise Instrument, the earliest artifact specifying the invitation and review procedure. Retain the existing problem frame: supported choice and ordinary assistance independent of participation remain the objectives. Add a prerequisite arrangement check before any human review invitation:

Specify how someone can obtain whatever ordinary assistance is available without entering the exercise, giving a reason for refusal or having participation status used in assistance decisions. Review must not occupy the staff or device capacity needed for that assistance. Role separation may be proposed only where capacity and responsibilities are accepted; another staff member must not be presumed available. If independence cannot be supported, defer the review rather than make assistance contingent on completing it.

Add external blank fields for assistance/review role arrangement, capacity boundary, unresolved conflict, proposed correction and accountable human decision. Record arrangement-level issues only. Do not record who refused, reasons for refusal, waiting-time traces or individual choice histories. DEPENDENCY MODEL A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning. STATE MODEL Maintain independent fields: Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided. Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability. STATUS AND PUBLIC DECISION
This integrated Evaluate amendment is a provisional rehearsal artifact, not human-approved requirements. Sequence 44 supplies blank instruments; sequence 59 supplies bounded evaluation claims; sequence 62 supplies one hypothetical objection about a librarian simultaneously providing assistance and inviting review. No observation, approval, executed check, measured outcome or demonstrated proficiency exists. Field evidence remains pending.

EARLIEST REVISION
Request one revision of Instrument sequence 44. Its invitation procedure specifies optional participation but lacks a prerequisite check for practical independence from assistance. The Understand objective already supports refusal and assistance independent of participation; the scenario does not invalidate that frame. Retain the candidate and sequence 59's claim limits. This event alone warrants no prototype change. Do not treat the requested revision as completed or approved.

INSERT BEFORE THE HUMAN REVIEW INVITATION
Before inviting participation, describe how someone can obtain whatever ordinary assistance is available without entering the exercise, explaining refusal or having participation status used in assistance decisions. Identify assistance and review responsibilities and the staff/device capacity each would use. Do not presume a second staff member, spare computer or available assistance.
Role separation is one possible arrangement only where responsibilities and capacity are accepted. The arrangement must protect ordinary assistance from displacement by review. If practical independence or capacity cannot be supported, defer the review. A statement that participation is optional is insufficient by itself. Paper or spoken review remains subject to this same prerequisite.

ARRANGEMENT CHECK — BLANK EXTERNAL RECORD
Material revision and proposed setting: pending.
Available ordinary-assistance route and its limits: unknown.
Assistance/review roles and accepted responsibilities: unassigned/pending.
Staff and device capacity boundary: unknown.
How refusal avoids an assistance consequence: pending review.
Unresolved conflict, dissent and alternative interpretation: pending.
Proposed correction or deferral: pending.
Accountable human decision, evidence basis and limits: pending.
Record arrangement-level issues only. Exclude who refused, refusal reasons, waiting-time traces, personal circumstances and individual choice histories. Record handling requires human agreement. Deferral leaves evidence absent; it establishes neither patron inability nor successful protection.

EVALUATION CONSEQUENCES
Add the arrangement check to the prerequisites for voluntary interaction and comparison review. Preserve sequence 44's separate technical checks and sequence 59's claim ledger. An executed technical check could support only the checked behavior in its stated configuration. It cannot establish acceptable participation, device-wide erasure or benefit.
Any later voluntary accounts may inform correction of wording, access, privacy or burden. Cooperation, completion, stopping and revision alone cannot establish agency or understanding. Apparent ease may reflect obligation, politeness, curiosity, prompting, familiarity, condition order or clearer service wording. Difficulty may reflect language, device or service barriers. Preserve contrary interpretations and offer correction without requiring an explanation.
Immediate revision under the same prompts cannot establish transfer. A separately reviewed inquiry needs another fictional task with comparable demands and documented support; retention also needs an agreed delay and feasible method. Do not expand tracking to obtain stronger claims. Access coverage, workload feasibility and all learning outcomes remain unknown.

HUMAN AND SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS
Humans: accessible refusal and interpretation correction; bounded accepted duties; authority to reject the tool or defer review. Accountable review must examine whether arrangements support independence in practice. No role assignment or approval exists.
Systems and materials: distinguish exercise from assistance before invitation; retain fictional fixed choices, descriptive correction, concealment, clearing and stopping. Add no sensitive-data entry, participation tracking, patron scores, assistance allocation or automatic handoffs. Keep arrangement records outside the candidate.

ALTERNATIVES AND NEXT ACTION
Compare the same fictional notice through paper or conversation with available staff only under reviewed arrangements. Writing is optional; folding paper conceals but does not erase it. Changing medium alone does not resolve the role conflict. Direct assistance, clearer service notices or no exercise may be preferable.
Carry this insertion into one Instrument revision and present it with the existing ledger for accountable framing, access, privacy, record-handling and workload review. Keep technical verification, voluntary interaction evidence and any separate pilot decision pending. This rehearsal establishes no launch authorization or efficacy.

All human gates, technical findings and field evidence remain pending.
objections: Hypothetical patron dissent from sequence 62: declining the person who provides help may not feel safe.
Hypothetical librarian dissent: another reviewer cannot be presumed available; deferral must remain feasible.
Rivals include obligation, politeness, curiosity, prompting and clearer wording; staffing, demand, perceived pressure and workable arrangements remain unknown.

The candidate must retain fictional choices, correction and privacy controls without allocating assistance, tracking participation or issuing scores.
tradeoffs: Protecting ordinary assistance may reduce opportunities to collect review evidence.
Role separation may reduce pressure but requires feasible, accepted capacity.
Minimal collection protects discretion while limiting explanations of nonparticipation.

These implement the revision prompted by sequence 27, already adopted in sequence 29; no further earlier-stage revision is requested. Discoverability under magnification remains unverified. STATE AND TRANSITION CONTRACT One transition function manages current draft, optional description, optional prompt, activity and visibility. No event history is maintained. Conceal removes the planning subtree, including selections, descriptions and prompts, while retaining current-session values. Explicit reveal restores visibility without changing activity or focusing the description. Clear removes draft values, description and prompt; it preserves paused or stopped activity and confirms the limits of removal. It does not create another draft. New draft explicitly creates undecided choices while preserving activity. Resume is a separate explicit action. Stop disables planning while leaving privacy controls available. Optional confusion or interruption pauses planning. Keep retains choices; revise-and-resume explicitly permits editing; leave undecided changes both choices without resuming. Stopping needs no completion judgment. Startup makes no inference about earlier drafts and does not claim detected loss. Browser restoration still requires inspection. HUMAN REQUIREMENTS Patrons must be able to decline the exercise, use selected, spoken or paper participation, correct choices and challenge missing actions without disclosing personal circumstances. Review arrangements must address relevant languages and access needs rather than presume them. Librarians and service owners need bounded time and authority to reject assistance promises or added workload. These roles are proposed, not accepted assignments. SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS The candidate uses deterministic descriptions and temporary current-state memory. It contains no free-text field, persistent storage, analytics, exports, transmissions, service requests or consequential judgments. Provision stays unknown. Removing a display is not a guarantee about browser, operating-system or device records. Accessibility, restoration and privacy behavior need technical verification and human interaction testing. NON-AI REVIEW MATERIAL The visible paper-card section supplies the same fictional notice, approach/action choices and keep/change/undecided/pause/stop options. Copying it to paper, pointing or ordinary conversation with available staff are alternatives. Writing is optional and fictional only. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it; discreet handling needs review. Clearer service notices may remove the need for this tool. Staff availability is unknown. PROPOSED VERIFICATION — UNPERFORMED Use fictional selections to check: correction after description leaves no stale output; conceal after an interruption removes all plan-bearing content from visual, keyboard and accessibility exposure; clear while stopped followed by new draft remains stopped. Also examine keyboard discovery from inside planning, narrow and magnified reflow, neutral focus, reveal without resumption, reload/restoration and storage/network behavior. Record version, scripted transition, expected behavior and actual technical findings only after execution; keep patron histories out of the candidate. EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES Accountable patron and librarian review must examine framing, access, privacy, missing actions and workload before approval. Interaction testing and resolution of the framing gate must precede any pilot. All human review, technical checks and field evidence remain pending. Preserve objections, including preference for direct assistance, paper, service redesign or no tool. Any later voluntary learning inquiry needs a different fictional task and documented prompts/support. Completion, speed and one corrected plan cannot establish retention or transfer. Prompt copying, familiarity, language demands, fatigue and service improvements remain rival explanations. NEXT ACTION Review this concrete candidate and paired paper material against the proposed transition checks; obtain accountable human review without implying approval from this rehearsal. SCREEN ORDER AND ACCESS Place a short strip labeled “Privacy and stopping” before planning content and first among interactive controls in keyboard order. Use neutral buttons: “Conceal draft,” “Clear draft,” and “Stop exercise.” Keep applicable actions accessible during active, paused, stopped and concealed states; clearing must remain available without revealing content. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.” Approach choices: consider online; check for paper; check for staffed help; availability unknown; none works; undecided. Next-action choices: examine the notice; ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available; check another route; my action is not listed; undecided. Both default to undecided. No explanation is required for a missing action. “Describe my draft” optionally presents fixed text describing current selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” Visible descriptions update immediately after correction. No preferred route, praise, score or completion judgment is allowed. PRIVACY AND FOCUS TRANSITIONS Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and all choice-specific messages, including interruption output, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Move focus to a neutral status: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Provide explicit reveal, clear and stop controls. Move focus to: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Preserve paused or stopped activity. Do not recreate a draft automatically. A new undecided draft requires explicit action; resuming also requires explicit action. Focus destinations must remain available and understandable without exposing choices. Use temporary current-draft memory only: no free text, history, analytics, persistent storage, exports, transmissions or automatic staff requests. All implementation boundaries require verification. OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY Offer separate invitations to try a confusing notice or rehearse an interruption. Neither unlocks assistance or finishing. Confusion repeats that confirmation and help availability remain unresolved. Interruption states: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue,” and pauses activity. Offer keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; privacy controls remain available. No automatic recovery or inferred intention is permitted. If draft loss is known, disclose it and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices. NON-AI COMPARISON Prepare a paper card with the same notice, approach and action choices, correction, uncertainty, pause and stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it; discreet handling needs review. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices remain alternatives. Staff capacity is unknown; reviewers may prefer an alternative or reject the tool. REVIEW AND NEXT ACTION Prepare this revised screen outline, paper card and fictional transition checks. Proposed checks cover keyboard discovery during interruption, magnified reflow, neutral focus, complete concealment, stale descriptions, clear while stopped, and storage/transmission boundaries. INSERT BEFORE THE HUMAN REVIEW INVITATION Before inviting participation, describe how someone can obtain whatever ordinary assistance is available without entering the exercise, explaining refusal or having participation status used in assistance decisions. Identify assistance and review responsibilities and the staff/device capacity each would use. Do not presume a second staff member, spare computer or available assistance. EVALUATION CONSEQUENCES Add the arrangement check to the prerequisites for voluntary interaction and comparison review.
