Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate. PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action. DEPENDENCY MODEL A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning. STATE MODEL Maintain independent fields: Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided. Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability. Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action. Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion. REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan. Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise. ADOPTED MODEL REVISION Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame. LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed. NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates. EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence. Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted. NEXT ACTION Use this model to prepare a small screen outline, matching paper card and dependency questions sheet for review. Sequence 4 identifies route reality, privacy and assistance capacity as unresolved. Sequence 6 challenges the assumption that three offered routes constitute meaningful choice. The seed supplies the fictional task and restrictions. No participant observations, human approvals or field results exist. PROBLEM FRAME Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping. ADOPTED REVISION The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. These are working requirements awaiting human review, not approved commitments. FICTIONAL REVIEW MATERIAL Exercise text: “Imagine a made-up library event called Community Drawing Hour. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.” Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline: • Approach: online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / pause or stop. • Next action: examine the fictional notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / leave undecided / stop. A different fictional action may be expressed, but writing is optional. • Change prompt: “The shared computer session ends before you continue, or the instruction remains confusing. Keep, change or abandon your plan.” Do not require recovery or an explanation. • Feedback example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability remains unknown. You can change or stop this plan.” Feedback describes explicit choices only; it cannot establish access, readiness, consent, skill or transfer. PRIVACY AND ACCESS BOUNDARIES Use no real passwords, identifiers, contact details, account information or service records. Concealment must explain that fictional notes remain in the current session. Clearing must remove candidate-held notes and visibly confirm removal; it must not promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Examine what appears after interruption and session ending. Wording, languages, keyboard access and other participation arrangements require review. Paper also needs readable wording, physical access and discreet handling. COMPARISON AND OPEN QUESTIONS Compare the candidate with the same paper card and an ordinary conversation with available staff. Review may favor either alternative or reject the workbench. Unknowns include actual route availability, assistance boundaries, staff capacity, language needs, shared-device behavior and whether another planning task is wanted. Preserve objections even if other reviewers favor the candidate. EVIDENCE PLAN — ALL PENDING Proposed review questions: Can reviewers identify an acceptable action, including no action? Do route labels imply unavailable provision? Can they revise, conceal, clear and stop with understandable consequences? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens does each approach introduce? Use fictional content only and retain contrary accounts. Difficulty could reflect instructions or unavailable opportunities; apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity. Later transfer would need separate evidence in another fictional task and cannot be inferred from completion here. NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE Prepare the paired paper card and screen outline from these working requirements, plus a route-and-assistance questions sheet. Then arrange patron and librarian review of the problem framing, refusal paths, access arrangements, privacy wording and workload boundaries. Record proposed changes and unresolved dissent without declaring consensus. Advancement requires accountable human review of this framing; any interactive candidate subsequently requires human review and interaction testing before a pilot. Sequence 22 establishes retention and delegation boundaries. Sequence 27 supplies a hypothetical access challenge; sequence 29 revises placement, reflow and focus. No observed incident, runnable candidate, technical result, human approval or field evidence exists. The unresolved Understand review gate remains pending. IMPLEMENTATION CHALLENGE AND REFINEMENT Prominent controls and temporary memory describe intended behavior; they do not verify concealment, clearing or recovery. Independently implementing buttons can produce inconsistent combinations: a cleared paused draft may reappear on resume, or reveal may inadvertently resume activity. Diagnostic logging could also recreate prohibited interaction histories. Refine Build around a single explicit transition function and current-state rendering, with no event history. This implements the revised Design rather than requesting another earlier-stage revision. STATUS AND REVISION
Provisional integrated Instrument revision for public deliberation in a rehearsal, not approved requirements. Sequence 44 supplies the original sheets; 62 supplies an invented objection about one librarian providing assistance and inviting review; 64 requests this revision. This draft implements that request. No actual incident, observation, approval, executed check or measured outcome exists. Field evidence remains pending.

Instrument was the earliest affected artifact because it specified the invitation procedure. The supported-choice frame remains applicable. Retain Build sequence 37 and Evaluate sequence 59’s inference limits. No further earlier-stage revision or prototype change is requested from this scenario alone.

PURPOSE AND RECORD BOUNDARY
Examine acceptable choice, privacy, access and effort alongside alternatives. Keep instruments outside the candidate. Exclude real passwords, identifiers, contact details, account information, service records, personal circumstances, identifiable quotations, recordings, timing traces and patron choice histories. No eligibility, banking, legal or medical guidance, patron scores or deficit labels. Human agreement on record scope, access, handling and disposal remains pending.

SHEET 0 — REQUIRED BEFORE HUMAN INVITATIONS
Describe how someone can obtain whatever ordinary assistance is available without entering review, explaining refusal or having participation status used in assistance decisions. Identify assistance/review responsibilities and staff/device capacity. Review must not displace that assistance. Role separation is an option only with feasible capacity and accepted duties; presume neither another librarian nor a spare computer. If independence or capacity cannot be supported, defer human review and comparison, including paper or spoken review.

Blank external arrangement record:
Material revision and setting: pending.
Available assistance route and limits: unknown.
Assistance/review roles and accepted duties: unassigned/pending.
Staff/device capacity boundary: unknown.
How refusal avoids assistance consequences: pending review.
Conflict, dissent and rival interpretation: pending.
Correction or deferral: pending.
Accountable human decision, evidence basis and limits: pending.
Record arrangement-level issues only, never who refused or why. Deferral means evidence remains absent; it proves neither patron inability nor successful protection. A documented arrangement cannot establish that participation feels voluntary.

SHEET A — TECHNICAL VERIFICATION
Blank fields: Build revision 1, sequence 37; configuration; fictional script; expected behavior specified beforehand; actual finding: not performed; scope; issue; correction and affected recheck.
Priority scripts: describe then correct a selector, checking current output; describe then interrupt and conceal, checking visual, keyboard and accessibility exposure and neutral focus; stop then clear then create a draft, checking undecided choices and continued stopped activity. Also examine reveal without resumption, clear while paused, privacy discovery from planning, magnified/narrow reflow, restoration and storage/transmission in the proposed setting. Findings would support only executed behavior in that configuration, never benefit or device-wide erasure.

SHEET B — OPTIONAL HUMAN REVIEW
Use only after reviewed framing, access, privacy, record handling, Sheet 0 arrangements and applicable technical prerequisites. Prepare invitation wording identifying the reviewed assistance route separately, then explain that the fictional exercise, descriptions and practice are optional; paper, spoken participation, uncertainty and stopping require no explanation. Do not issue an invitation while that route or arrangement remains unresolved.
Blank fields: materials/configuration and support; issue category; non-identifying issue description; alternative interpretation; proposed change; dissent; correction opportunity and unresolved question. Examine misleading provision, refusal, privacy discovery, access burden and workload. Declining interpretation correction implies no agreement. Silence supplies no evidence of inability or acceptance.

SHEETS C/D — ALTERNATIVES, COVERAGE AND CLAIMS
Compare the same invented notice through the workbench, paper card or conversation with available staff only under Sheet 0 arrangements. Record wording, order, support, navigation/reading burden, correction, discretion, assistance demands and contrary accounts. Writing is optional; folding conceals paper but does not erase it. Paper alone does not resolve the role conflict. Direct assistance, clearer notices or no exercise remain possible recommendations.
Mark language, keyboard, magnification, other access and shared-device conditions as planned, checked within scope or unknown. Omit identifying detail and retain coverage gaps. Cooperation, completion, speed, help-seeking and revision cannot establish agency, equity or learning. Prompting, obligation, familiarity, order, fatigue and service clarification remain rivals. Transfer requires separate review and another fictional task with documented support; retention also needs an agreed delay and feasible method. Do not expand tracking to strengthen claims.

NEXT ACTION AND GATES
Present this revised packet with sequence 51’s whole-setting dossier and sequence 59’s claim ledger for accountable review. All roles, arrangements, technical findings and human decisions remain pending. Human invitations must wait for the prerequisites above; deployment and any pilot require their separate human gates. This draft establishes preparation only, not authorization or efficacy.

Sequence 24 integrates the dependency model and retention boundaries; sequence 20 separates supported planning from optional practice and learning inquiry. Sequence 27 supplies a hypothetical keyboard-and-magnification interruption exposing unspecified control placement and focus behavior. No incident, technical success, participant observation, approval or field result is asserted. REVISION AND SCOPE Revise Design once: replace nominal reachability with explicit placement, reflow and focus requirements. The dependency model and problem frame remain applicable; the earliest artifact needing this change is Design. The unresolved Understand human-review gate remains pending, without requesting another revision of Understand. SCREEN ORDER AND ACCESS Place a short strip labeled “Privacy and stopping” before planning content and first among interactive controls in keyboard order. Use neutral buttons: “Conceal draft,” “Clear draft,” and “Stop exercise.” Keep applicable actions accessible during active, paused, stopped and concealed states; clearing must remain available without revealing content. The layout must wrap controls without horizontal scrolling, clipping or overlap at magnification settings selected through human review. Any persistent positioning must not obscure controls, focused elements or task content. Review must examine discoverability from within the planning area, not merely from the initial screen. Do not rely on assumed shortcuts, devices or staff intervention. These are requirements to verify, not accessibility claims. FICTIONAL PLANNING CONTENT Opening: “Community Drawing Hour is invented. Its notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Real routes and assistance availability are unknown. Use fictional choices only.” Approach choices: consider online; check for paper; check for staffed help; availability unknown; none works; undecided. Next-action choices: examine the notice; ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available; check another route; my action is not listed; undecided. Both default to undecided. No explanation is required for a missing action. “Describe my draft” optionally presents fixed text describing current selections, followed by: “Availability remains unknown. No request has been sent. This description does not establish understanding, skill or real access.” Visible descriptions update immediately after correction. No preferred route, praise, score or completion judgment is allowed. PRIVACY AND FOCUS TRANSITIONS Conceal hides selectors, descriptions and all choice-specific messages, including interruption output, from visual, keyboard and assistive-technology access. Move focus to a neutral status: “Fictional content remains in this session.” Provide explicit reveal, clear and stop controls. Reveal restores visibility only; it must not resume activity automatically or announce a choice-specific summary. Clear removes candidate-held choices, descriptions and choice-specific messages. Move focus to: “The candidate-held draft was cleared. This does not establish removal of browser, operating-system or device records.” Preserve paused or stopped activity. Do not recreate a draft automatically. A new undecided draft requires explicit action; resuming also requires explicit action. Focus destinations must remain available and understandable without exposing choices. Use temporary current-draft memory only: no free text, history, analytics, persistent storage, exports, transmissions or automatic staff requests. All implementation boundaries require verification. OPTIONAL CHANGE AND RECOVERY Offer separate invitations to try a confusing notice or rehearse an interruption. Neither unlocks assistance or finishing. Confusion repeats that confirmation and help availability remain unresolved. Interruption states: “Imagine the shared-computer session ends before you continue,” and pauses activity. Offer keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; privacy controls remain available. No automatic recovery or inferred intention is permitted. If draft loss is known, disclose it and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct choices. NON-AI COMPARISON Prepare a paper card with the same notice, approach and action choices, correction, uncertainty, pause and stop. Pointing or speaking is sufficient; writing is optional and fictional only. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it; discreet handling needs review. Ordinary conversation with available staff and clearer service notices remain alternatives. Staff capacity is unknown; reviewers may prefer an alternative or reject the tool. REVIEW AND NEXT ACTION Prepare this revised screen outline, paper card and fictional transition checks. Proposed checks cover keyboard discovery during interruption, magnified reflow, neutral focus, complete concealment, stale descriptions, clear while stopped, and storage/transmission boundaries. None has been performed. Accountable patron and librarian review must examine framing, access, privacy, missing actions and workload before approved design. Separate any voluntary learning inquiry using another fictional task and documented support conditions; completion, speed or one revised plan cannot establish retention or transfer.","prototype_html":"","title":"Revised Design synthesis: discoverable privacy controls and supported choice"},"content_hash":"3f234e938602b268ec8f69c3c64e17b5fad30fe53fda30a65729cd72ee6aa306","id":"design","parent_revision":1,"revision":2,"trigger_seq":29},"evaluate":{"content":{"body":"STATUS AND PUBLIC DECISION This integrated Evaluate amendment is a provisional rehearsal artifact, not human-approved requirements. Its invitation procedure specifies optional participation but lacks a prerequisite check for practical independence from assistance. The Understand objective already supports refusal and assistance independent of participation; the scenario does not invalidate that frame. Retain the candidate and sequence 59's claim limits. This event alone warrants no prototype change. Do not treat the requested revision as completed or approved. INSERT BEFORE THE HUMAN REVIEW INVITATION Before inviting participation, describe how someone can obtain whatever ordinary assistance is available without entering the exercise, explaining refusal or having participation status used in assistance decisions. Identify assistance and review responsibilities and the staff/device capacity each would use. Do not presume a second staff member, spare computer or available assistance. Role separation is one possible arrangement only where responsibilities and capacity are accepted. The arrangement must protect ordinary assistance from displacement by review. If practical independence or capacity cannot be supported, defer the review. A statement that participation is optional is insufficient by itself. Paper or spoken review remains subject to this same prerequisite. ARRANGEMENT CHECK — BLANK EXTERNAL RECORD Material revision and proposed setting: pending. Available ordinary-assistance route and its limits: unknown. Assistance/review roles and accepted responsibilities: unassigned/pending. Staff and device capacity boundary: unknown. How refusal avoids an assistance consequence: pending review. Unresolved conflict, dissent and alternative interpretation: pending. Proposed correction or deferral: pending. Accountable human decision, evidence basis and limits: pending. Record arrangement-level issues only. Exclude who refused, refusal reasons, waiting-time traces, personal circumstances and individual choice histories. Record handling requires human agreement. Deferral leaves evidence absent; it establishes neither patron inability nor successful protection. EVALUATION CONSEQUENCES Add the arrangement check to the prerequisites for voluntary interaction and comparison review. Preserve sequence 44's separate technical checks and sequence 59's claim ledger. An executed technical check could support only the checked behavior in its stated configuration. It cannot establish acceptable participation, device-wide erasure or benefit. Any later voluntary accounts may inform correction of wording, access, privacy or burden. Cooperation, completion, stopping and revision alone cannot establish agency or understanding. Apparent ease may reflect obligation, politeness, curiosity, prompting, familiarity, condition order or clearer service wording. Difficulty may reflect language, device or service barriers. Preserve contrary interpretations and offer correction without requiring an explanation. Immediate revision under the same prompts cannot establish transfer. A separately reviewed inquiry needs another fictional task with comparable demands and documented support; retention also needs an agreed delay and feasible method. Do not expand tracking to obtain stronger claims. Access coverage, workload feasibility and all learning outcomes remain unknown. HUMAN AND SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS Humans: accessible refusal and interpretation correction; bounded accepted duties; authority to reject the tool or defer review. Accountable review must examine whether arrangements support independence in practice. No role assignment or approval exists. Systems and materials: distinguish exercise from assistance before invitation; retain fictional fixed choices, descriptive correction, concealment, clearing and stopping. Add no sensitive-data entry, participation tracking, patron scores, assistance allocation or automatic handoffs. Keep arrangement records outside the candidate. ALTERNATIVES AND NEXT ACTION Compare the same fictional notice through paper or conversation with available staff only under reviewed arrangements. Writing is optional; folding paper conceals but does not erase it. Changing medium alone does not resolve the role conflict. Direct assistance, clearer service notices or no exercise may be preferable. Carry this insertion into one Instrument revision and present it with the existing ledger for accountable framing, access, privacy, record-handling and workload review. Keep technical verification, voluntary interaction evidence and any separate pilot decision pending. SHEET 0 — REQUIRED BEFORE HUMAN INVITATIONS Describe how someone can obtain whatever ordinary assistance is available without entering review, explaining refusal or having participation status used in assistance decisions. SHEET A — TECHNICAL VERIFICATION Blank fields: Build revision 1, sequence 37; configuration; fictional script; expected behavior specified beforehand; actual finding: not performed; scope; issue; correction and affected recheck. SHEETS C/D — ALTERNATIVES, COVERAGE AND CLAIMS Compare the same invented notice through the workbench, paper card or conversation with available staff only under Sheet 0 arrangements. Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate. PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action. DEPENDENCY MODEL A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning. STATE MODEL Maintain independent fields: Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided. Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability. Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action. Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion. REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan. Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise. ADOPTED MODEL REVISION Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame. LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed. NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates. EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence. Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted. NEXT ACTION Use this model to prepare a small screen outline, matching paper card and dependency questions sheet for review. Sequence 4 identifies route reality, privacy and assistance capacity as unresolved. Sequence 6 challenges the assumption that three offered routes constitute meaningful choice. The seed supplies the fictional task and restrictions. No participant observations, human approvals or field results exist. PROBLEM FRAME Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping. ADOPTED REVISION The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. These are working requirements awaiting human review, not approved commitments. FICTIONAL REVIEW MATERIAL Exercise text: “Imagine a made-up library event called Community Drawing Hour. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.” Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline: • Approach: online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / pause or stop. • Next action: examine the fictional notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / leave undecided / stop. A different fictional action may be expressed, but writing is optional. • Change prompt: “The shared computer session ends before you continue, or the instruction remains confusing. Keep, change or abandon your plan.” Do not require recovery or an explanation. • Feedback example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability remains unknown. You can change or stop this plan.” Feedback describes explicit choices only; it cannot establish access, readiness, consent, skill or transfer. PRIVACY AND ACCESS BOUNDARIES Use no real passwords, identifiers, contact details, account information or service records. Concealment must explain that fictional notes remain in the current session. Clearing must remove candidate-held notes and visibly confirm removal; it must not promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Examine what appears after interruption and session ending. Wording, languages, keyboard access and other participation arrangements require review. Paper also needs readable wording, physical access and discreet handling. COMPARISON AND OPEN QUESTIONS Compare the candidate with the same paper card and an ordinary conversation with available staff. Review may favor either alternative or reject the workbench. Unknowns include actual route availability, assistance boundaries, staff capacity, language needs, shared-device behavior and whether another planning task is wanted. Preserve objections even if other reviewers favor the candidate. EVIDENCE PLAN — ALL PENDING Proposed review questions: Can reviewers identify an acceptable action, including no action? Do route labels imply unavailable provision? Can they revise, conceal, clear and stop with understandable consequences? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens does each approach introduce? Use fictional content only and retain contrary accounts. Difficulty could reflect instructions or unavailable opportunities; apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity. Later transfer would need separate evidence in another fictional task and cannot be inferred from completion here. NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE Prepare the paired paper card and screen outline from these working requirements, plus a route-and-assistance questions sheet. Then arrange patron and librarian review of the problem framing, refusal paths, access arrangements, privacy wording and workload boundaries. Record proposed changes and unresolved dissent without declaring consensus. Advancement requires accountable human review of this framing; any interactive candidate subsequently requires human review and interaction testing before a pilot. STATUS AND BASIS
Expert draft for public deliberation in a rehearsal, not approved requirements. Build sequence 37 separates activity, visibility and draft presence. Deploy sequence 51 proposes whole-setting gates and suspension. Evaluate sequence 59 limits inference. Instrument revision sequence 67 adds assistance independence and capacity checks before invitations. No executed checks, participant observations, human approvals or measured outcomes exist. Field evidence remains pending.

SYSTEMS CHALLENGE
A prerequisite arrangement check establishes a proposed starting condition, not continuing feasibility. Assistance demand, staff availability or a shared-computer session can change. The current packet does not specify when capacity must be reconsidered or how an optional review ends without creating a recovery duty. This is a specification gap to address in Refine, not an observed incident or grounds for another earlier-stage revision.

PROPOSED OPERATING CONTRACT
Before any separately authorized human review, specify which observable setting changes require reconsideration: loss of accepted reviewer availability, ordinary assistance needing the same staff/device capacity, or a changed device/hosting configuration. Use setting-level conditions; do not monitor patron behavior, queue histories or refusal patterns.
When a relevant condition changes, pause new invitations and reassess assistance independence. Defer affected review if the arrangement cannot be supported. Do not presume another librarian, computer or assistance route. If even this check exceeds accepted workload, review should remain deferred. Record only the arrangement issue and proposed disposition outside the candidate under an agreed handling process.
Existing participants must retain the choice to stop. Capacity reassessment must not compel them to finish, disclose choices or accept another medium. No operational responsibility is assigned by this draft.

RECOVERY BOUNDARIES
Distinguish ending the exercise, hiding its content and removing its draft. In sequence 37, stopping disables planning while leaving choices visible; concealment retains choices in the session; clearing removes the candidate-held draft. Review whether these separate consequences are understandable, including after interruption. Do not infer that stopping expresses a wish to erase, and do not describe stopping as a privacy guarantee.
If a session ends, the candidate provides no reliable recovery commitment. Do not reconstruct inferred choices or promise staff-assisted restoration. A fresh undecided draft, paper/spoken planning or stopping are proposed alternatives only under feasible reviewed arrangements. Restoration, focus and concealment behavior require actual technical verification. Clearing cannot establish device-wide erasure.

NON-TRAINING LEVERS
Review the fictional notice's unexplained confirmation wording before adding prompts or practice. Prepare a clearly labeled revised fictional notice with an explicit next-step description for comparison; it supplies no real service guidance. Separately ask accountable service owners to examine real route wording and provision outside this rehearsal, without supplying personal service records.
Consider simpler notices, removal of unnecessary planning steps, bounded assistance procedures and discreet paper handling. These changes may reduce the need for a workbench. Patron training must not be the default response to unavailable routes, confusing service design or insufficient staffing.

HUMAN AND SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS
Humans: accessible refusal and correction, authority to defer or reject review, and accepted limits on assistance and recovery duties. Language and access arrangements remain unspecified. Silence establishes no agreement.
Systems/materials: retain fictional choices, descriptive correction, visible conceal/clear controls and independent activity states. Add no sensitive-data entry, scores, tracking, assistance allocation or automatic referrals. Keep configuration and arrangement records outside the candidate; exclude patron histories and personal circumstances.

REVIEWABLE NEXT ACTION
Add a blank operating card to the Refine packet: material/configuration revision; accepted capacity boundary; setting changes requiring reassessment; proposed pause/deferral response; recovery limitations; dissent; accountable human decision. Every acceptance and finding field remains pending. Review the card alongside sequence 67's prerequisites and sequence 51's dossier before human invitations.
Retain sequence 59's inference limits. Apparent improvement could reflect clearer wording, prompting, familiarity or perceived obligation. Completion cannot establish agency, actual access, retention or transfer. Compare paper, conversation with available staff, clearer notices and no exercise; changing medium alone does not resolve capacity conflicts. No launch or efficacy follows from this draft.

Sequence 51 proposes suspension authority without establishing feasible coverage. Refine the operating contract to address changed conditions and recovery without assuming spare staff, devices or patron training. This is a proposed requirement, not a discovered failure or approved arrangement. Technical verification, human review and field evidence remain pending.

Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate. PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action. DEPENDENCY MODEL A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning. STATE MODEL Maintain independent fields: Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided. Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability. Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action. Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion. REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan. Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise. ADOPTED MODEL REVISION Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame. LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed. NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. PROBLEM FRAME Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping. ADOPTED REVISION The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. These are working requirements awaiting human review, not approved commitments. FICTIONAL REVIEW MATERIAL Exercise text: “Imagine a made-up library event called Community Drawing Hour. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.” Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline: • Approach: online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / pause or stop. • Next action: examine the fictional notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / leave undecided / stop. Keep, change or abandon your plan.” Do not require recovery or an explanation. • Feedback example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability remains unknown. Field evidence remains pending. SYSTEMS CHALLENGE A prerequisite arrangement check establishes a proposed starting condition, not continuing feasibility. Assistance demand, staff availability or a shared-computer session can change. The current packet does not specify when capacity must be reconsidered or how an optional review ends without creating a recovery duty. This is a specification gap to address in Refine, not an observed incident or grounds for another earlier-stage revision. PROPOSED OPERATING CONTRACT Before any separately authorized human review, specify which observable setting changes require reconsideration: loss of accepted reviewer availability, ordinary assistance needing the same staff/device capacity, or a changed device/hosting configuration. Use setting-level conditions; do not monitor patron behavior, queue histories or refusal patterns. When a relevant condition changes, pause new invitations and reassess assistance independence. If even this check exceeds accepted workload, review should remain deferred. Record only the arrangement issue and proposed disposition outside the candidate under an agreed handling process. Existing participants must retain the choice to stop. Capacity reassessment must not compel them to finish, disclose choices or accept another medium. No operational responsibility is assigned by this draft. RECOVERY BOUNDARIES Distinguish ending the exercise, hiding its content and removing its draft. STATUS AND BASIS
Expert draft for public deliberation in a rehearsal, not approved requirements. Build sequence 37 supplies fixed choices and descriptive output. Evaluate sequence 59 separates adaptation, transfer and retention. Instrument sequence 67 requires practical assistance independence before invitations. Systems sequence 73 proposes capacity reassessment and service improvements before training. No observations, approvals, executed checks or demonstrated proficiency exist. Field evidence remains pending.

LEARNING CHALLENGE
Repeating the same selectors can rehearse the interface without practicing how to approach an unfamiliar notice. The current description accurately echoes choices; it does not diagnose reasoning or identify a learning need. Preserve its modest purpose. A finished plan, corrected selector or confident response cannot establish competence.

PROPOSED REFINE REQUIREMENT
Prepare a separate optional practice card for human review, rather than adding compulsory steps to the candidate. State one possible practice aim: notice an unresolved requirement and choose a way to address it while retaining control. Seeking support, remaining undecided and stopping remain valid. The aim is a proposed responsibility for the exercise, not an observed patron capability.

REVIEWABLE PRACTICE CARD
Start with the existing invented Community Drawing Hour notice. Invite, without requiring an explanation: “Is anything unclear? You may point, select, speak, leave undecided or stop.” Offer examining the wording, checking whether help or another route exists, and an unlisted action. No response unlocks assistance.

Optional variation: “An invented Community Story Hour notice says ‘choose a session before requesting a place,’ but lists no sessions.” This supplies no real service guidance. Ask what next action the person would consider. Change the uncertainty rather than merely the event name. Use this as practice material only; it is not an established transfer assessment or equivalent task.

Allow another attempt only if wanted. Invite keeping, changing or rejecting a plan; do not prescribe repetition counts. Apply sequence 73's capacity boundary and defer practice when it competes with ordinary assistance. No spare staff or device is presumed.

DESCRIPTIVE FEEDBACK CONTRACT
Describe the selected action and the unresolved feature separately. Example: “Your draft selects checking another route. This fictional notice still lists no sessions. Another route's availability is unknown. You may keep, change or stop.” Use this wording only when that selection was explicit.

Do not claim that the person noticed the missing information, understood the notice or chose correctly. A cue may help someone reconsider; it may also supply what they had not identified. Review whether feedback is useful, confusing or burdensome, and permit rejection without an explanation. Different acceptable actions must not be ranked.

EVIDENCE AND SUPPORT BOUNDARIES
A voluntary account or action could support a narrow description of what occurred under stated conditions. Distinguish choosing after a cue from identifying uncertainty before that cue. Record material wording and support arrangements outside the candidate under agreed handling; do not preserve patron response histories or introduce tracking.

A later inquiry about transfer would need separately reviewed fictional material with changed surface features, comparable demands and documented support. Transfer may include appropriate help-seeking; independence is not the criterion. Retention additionally requires an agreed delay and feasible voluntary method. Neither exists. If privacy and capacity boundaries cannot support the inquiry, leave the claim unknown.

NON-AI OPTION, DISSENT AND RIVALS
Use the same optional card on paper or through conversation with available staff; writing is unnecessary. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it. Clearer notices, direct assistance or no exercise may be preferable. Changing medium does not resolve sequence 67's role conflict. Preserve objections to practicing at all. Prompting, familiarity, language demands, fatigue, obligation and clearer service wording remain rival explanations for apparent improvement.

NEXT ACTION
Present this optional card and feedback contract alongside sequences 59, 67 and 73 for accountable patron and librarian review. Resolve framing, access, privacy, record handling and workload prerequisites before invitations. Review may omit practice entirely. No earlier artifact revision is requested; no prototype change, launch authorization or learning success is asserted.

response.challenged_assumption: Repeated selector use and revision under unchanged prompts constitute deliberate practice or demonstrate a strategy that transfers to unfamiliar service notices.
response.decision: Propose the optional practice card and feedback contract for accountable review. Retain current descriptive output and all existing gates; keep practice invitations, retention and transfer claims pending. Request no earlier-stage revision.
drawbacks: Optional practice adds reading and review effort.
Fictional adaptation cannot establish actual service access.
Current records cannot establish individual retention.
flourishing: Agency and dignity: patrons choose whether practice has value and can reject feedback.
Access and belonging: supported, paper and spoken participation retain equal standing.
Sustainable workload and learning/transfer: bound review effort and investigate adaptation without requiring independence.
human_capabilities: Patrons need optional selected, spoken or paper responses, correction and stopping without explanation.
Reviewers need to distinguish explicit task actions from inferred understanding, retention and transfer.
Librarians need accepted workload limits and authority to omit practice or defer review.
response.message: Learning scientist Refine draft: sequence 37 describes selected choices but cannot reveal whether someone recognizes ambiguity or can adapt a strategy. Sequence 59 correctly limits learning claims; sequence 67 protects practical refusal; sequence 73 prioritizes service barriers over training. I challenge treating repeated selector use as deliberate practice. Propose an optional practice card with varied fictional demands, descriptive feedback and explicit support boundaries. This is an expert draft, not an approved requirement. Human review and field evidence remain pending.
objections: Hypothetical patron dissent: “I need help with the notice, not another exercise.”
Rivals include prompt copying, familiarity, language demands, perceived obligation and clearer wording.
Unknowns include practice demand, access arrangements, staff capacity and a feasible retention method.
risks: Practice could become an unofficial prerequisite for assistance.
Echoed selections could be mistaken for diagnostic feedback.
Service barriers could be reframed as patron learning deficits.
system_capabilities: Keep descriptions tied to explicit choices; infer no skill, intention or readiness.
Keep practice separate from assistance and add no scores, histories or automatic advancement.
Preserve concealment, clearing and stopping; mark support conditions and absent evidence explicitly.
tradeoffs: Prompts support participation but limit claims about adaptation without those prompts.
Variation can expose strategy use while introducing language and task differences.
Minimal records protect discretion while limiting longitudinal inference.

Sequences 4 and 6 identify service barriers and meaningful refusal. Sequence 8 incorporates those into Understand. Sequence 13 separates plan preference from provision and challenges incomplete concealment. No participant observations, approvals, demonstrated proficiency or field results exist. Modeling does not satisfy the pending Understand review gate. PURPOSE AND BOUNDARY Model how an adult might choose an acceptable next action for the invented Community Drawing Hour while retaining control and manageable effort. The fictional notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and an unexplained instruction, “confirm your place.” The candidate cannot register anyone, establish real routes, reserve assistance or resolve that instruction through invented advice. Supported choice may include no action. DEPENDENCY MODEL A desired action depends on an opportunity: comprehensible service information, a usable route, suitable device conditions and assistance when wanted. These conditions are unknown. Service owners control notices and routes; library staff define assistance boundaries; device operators influence session behavior. None of their participation or resources is presumed. Investigate these conditions before attributing difficulty to patron learning. STATE MODEL Maintain independent fields: Preference: online / check paper / check staffed help / unknown / none works / undecided. Provision: unknown throughout this rehearsal; selections never confirm availability. Next action: examine the notice / ask what “confirm” means if help exists / check another route / undecided / another optional fictional action. Session visibility: visible / concealed. Content presence: draft present / cleared or lost. Activity: active / paused / stopped. Interruption is an event, not evidence of abandonment or completion. REVIEWABLE TRANSITIONS Choosing or correcting changes only explicit draft choices and their description. Confusion offers keep, revise, leave undecided or stop; it provides no unverified registration procedure. An interruption offers the same control plus conceal or clear, without requiring staff or automatic resumption. If content is lost, disclose the loss and offer a fresh undecided draft or stopping; never reconstruct an inferred plan. Stopping ends the exercise without a completion judgment. While content remains, conceal and clear stay accessible. Conceal hides choices, optional notes and every derived summary together; the remaining view states that fictional content remains in the session. Explicit reveal restores visibility. Clear removes candidate-held choices, notes and summaries and visibly confirms its scope. It cannot promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Clearing while stopped must not restart the exercise. ADOPTED MODEL REVISION Sequence 13's challenge changes the privacy requirement from hiding notes to hiding all plan-bearing displays. Review must also examine feedback, interruption messages and reveal behavior. This is a meaningful requirement revision, with technical verification pending; it does not require rewriting the earlier problem frame. LEARNING HYPOTHESIS AND FEEDBACK A possible learning mechanism is practicing how to identify ambiguity, check an opportunity, seek help and change direction. Optional descriptive feedback could make an explicit choice easier to reconsider; effectiveness is unknown. Example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability is unknown. You may change, leave undecided or stop.” Do not infer skill, consent, readiness or transfer. No compulsory writing, explanation or reflection is required. Later adaptation would need a different fictional task and separate evidence, including whether support was still needed. NON-AI AND SERVICE OPTIONS Prepare a paper card with the same uncertainty, next-action, revision and stop choices. An ordinary conversation with available staff is another option. Examine readable wording, physical access and discreet paper handling. Also investigate clearer notices and verified route information; improving a service may remove the need for a planning tool. Review may favor an alternative or reject all candidates. EVIDENCE AND HUMAN GATES — PENDING Proposed comparison questions: Can reviewers find an acceptable action, including stopping? Do labels imply provision? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens arise? Can fictional content be corrected, concealed completely and cleared after interruption? Retain contrary accounts and distinguish task familiarity, reviewer prompting and service barriers from any learning explanation. Completion and speed are insufficient evidence. Unknowns include route existence, staffing windows, language arrangements, accessibility needs, shared-device behavior and demand for this tool. Accountable patron and librarian review must address framing, privacy, access and workload before approved design or a pilot. Subsequent technical checks and human interaction testing remain required. No recruitment, review, launch or efficacy is asserted. NEXT ACTION Use this model to prepare a small screen outline, matching paper card and dependency questions sheet for review. PROBLEM FRAME Investigate what enables adults to choose an acceptable next action for an unfamiliar service while retaining control, privacy and manageable effort. Barriers may lie in service design, available support, language or device access. Independent online completion is not the objective. A reasonable outcome can be seeking help, checking availability, leaving a plan undecided or stopping. ADOPTED REVISION The draft interaction must include “availability unknown,” “none works for me,” and “pause or stop,” without requiring a reason. Next actions may be selected, spoken, written or undecided. This changes both the interaction and its review criteria: a finished plan is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of supported choice. These are working requirements awaiting human review, not approved commitments. FICTIONAL REVIEW MATERIAL Exercise text: “Imagine a made-up library event called Community Drawing Hour. Its example notice offers morning or afternoon attendance and says ‘confirm your place’ without explaining how. This exercise cannot register anyone. Online, paper and staffed routes are possibilities to examine; their real availability is unknown.” Planning card, usable on paper or as a later screen outline: • Approach: online / check for paper / check for staffed help / availability unknown / none works / pause or stop. • Next action: examine the fictional notice / ask what ‘confirm’ means if help is available / check whether another route exists / leave undecided / stop. A different fictional action may be expressed, but writing is optional. • Change prompt: “The shared computer session ends before you continue, or the instruction remains confusing. Keep, change or abandon your plan.” Do not require recovery or an explanation. • Feedback example: “Your draft selects checking for paper registration. Its availability remains unknown. You can change or stop this plan.” Feedback describes explicit choices only; it cannot establish access, readiness, consent, skill or transfer. PRIVACY AND ACCESS BOUNDARIES Use no real passwords, identifiers, contact details, account information or service records. Concealment must explain that fictional notes remain in the current session. Clearing must remove candidate-held notes and visibly confirm removal; it must not promise removal of browser, operating-system or device records. Examine what appears after interruption and session ending. Wording, languages, keyboard access and other participation arrangements require review. Paper also needs readable wording, physical access and discreet handling. COMPARISON AND OPEN QUESTIONS Compare the candidate with the same paper card and an ordinary conversation with available staff. Review may favor either alternative or reject the workbench. Unknowns include actual route availability, assistance boundaries, staff capacity, language needs, shared-device behavior and whether another planning task is wanted. Preserve objections even if other reviewers favor the candidate. EVIDENCE PLAN — ALL PENDING Proposed review questions: Can reviewers identify an acceptable action, including no action? Do route labels imply unavailable provision? Can they revise, conceal, clear and stop with understandable consequences? What reading, privacy and assistance burdens does each approach introduce? Use fictional content only and retain contrary accounts. Difficulty could reflect instructions or unavailable opportunities; apparent ease could reflect prior familiarity. Later transfer would need separate evidence in another fictional task and cannot be inferred from completion here. NEXT ACTION AND HUMAN GATE Prepare the paired paper card and screen outline from these working requirements, plus a route-and-assistance questions sheet. Then arrange patron and librarian review of the problem framing, refusal paths, access arrangements, privacy wording and workload boundaries. Record proposed changes and unresolved dissent without declaring consensus. Advancement requires accountable human review of this framing; any interactive candidate subsequently requires human review and interaction testing before a pilot. STATUS AND BASIS
Provisional integrated Refine artifact for public deliberation in a rehearsal, not approved requirements. Sequence 67 implements the invitation revision prompted by hypothetical objection 62. Sequence 73 proposes ongoing capacity reassessment and recovery limits; sequence 75 proposes separate optional strategy practice. No observations, executed checks, approvals, measured outcomes or demonstrated proficiency exist. Field evidence remains pending.

STAGE DECISION
Add an operating card to review preparation and a separate optional practice card. Retain Build 37, Deploy 51’s whole-setting gates and Evaluate 59’s claim limits. These additions specify Refine responsibilities; no supplied finding warrants another earlier-stage revision. Do not add practice steps to the candidate. Review may omit practice or reject the workbench entirely.

OPERATING CARD — BLANK EXTERNAL RECORD
Material revision and proposed configuration: pending.
Available ordinary-assistance route and limits: unknown.
Assistance/review roles, accepted duties and capacity boundary: unassigned/pending.
Setting changes requiring reassessment: proposed below; acceptance pending.
Pause, deferral and recovery arrangements: pending review.
Dissent, rival interpretation and proposed correction: pending.
Accountable human decision, evidence basis and limits: pending.
Record handling and disposal: pending human agreement.
Exclude identities, personal circumstances, refusal records, recordings, timing traces and patron choice histories.

PROPOSED CHANGE RESPONSE
Reconsider arrangements when accepted reviewer availability ends, ordinary assistance needs the same staff/device capacity, or device/hosting configuration changes. Use setting-level conditions, without monitoring patron behavior or queues. Pause new invitations; reassess assistance independence and applicable technical gates. Defer affected review when capacity or independence cannot be supported. If reassessment itself exceeds accepted workload, keep review deferred. Presume neither spare staff nor computers. Existing participants retain the choice to stop without finishing, explaining choices or accepting another medium. Deferral leaves evidence absent; it proves neither inability nor successful protection.

RECOVERY CONTRACT
Stopping disables planning but leaves a visible draft. Concealment hides planning content while retaining current-session choices. Clearing removes the candidate-held draft and does not establish device-wide erasure. Explain these consequences separately; do not infer that stopping requests deletion. Session loss creates no reliable recovery commitment. Offer a fresh undecided draft, reviewed paper/spoken planning or stopping only under feasible arrangements. Do not reconstruct choices or promise staff restoration. Focus, restoration, complete concealment, correction and clear-while-stopped behavior remain untested.

OPTIONAL PRACTICE CARD
Possible aim: notice unresolved information and consider an acceptable next action while retaining control. Start with the invented Community Drawing Hour notice. Ask: “Is anything unclear? You may point, select, speak, remain undecided or stop.” Examining wording, checking whether help or another route exists, and an unlisted action are legitimate options. No response unlocks assistance.
Optional variation: “An invented Community Story Hour notice says ‘choose a session before requesting a place,’ but lists no sessions.” Invite a next action only if wanted. This changes the uncertainty; it is practice material, not an equivalent or validated transfer assessment. Repetition is optional and subject to the operating card.
Feedback describes an explicit selection and unresolved wording separately: “Your draft selects checking another route. This fictional notice lists no sessions. Another route’s availability is unknown. You may keep, change or stop.” Do not infer recognition, understanding or correctness. Permit rejection without explanation. Document wording and support arrangements, never individual response histories. Cued actions cannot establish uncued adaptation, retention or transfer.

ALTERNATIVES AND REQUIREMENTS
Compare paper or conversation with available staff using the same fictional material; writing is unnecessary. Folding conceals paper but does not erase it. Changing medium does not resolve role conflicts. Also review clearer fictional notices, fewer planning steps, direct assistance or no exercise before proposing training.
Humans need accessible refusal and correction, accepted workload limits and authority to defer or reject. Systems must preserve fictional choices and privacy controls without sensitive-data entry, guidance outside scope, scores, tracking or automatic handoffs. Actual route provision, access coverage and staff capacity remain unknown.

NEXT ACTION AND GATES
Present the operating card and optional practice material alongside Instrument 67, Deploy 51 and Evaluate 59 for accountable framing, access, privacy, record-handling and workload review. Perform scoped technical checks under agreed arrangements before voluntary interaction review. Preserve contrary accounts and rival explanations. Human invitations and any separate pilot remain gated; this rehearsal authorizes no launch or efficacy claim.

drawbacks: Reassessment and practice review require unconfirmed staff capacity.
Deferral can leave comparison and learning evidence unavailable.
Fictional planning cannot establish actual service access.
flourishing: Agency and dignity: uncertainty, refusal, correction and stopping remain legitimate without justification.
Access and belonging: review language, device, paper and spoken participation without privileging independent online completion.
Sustainable workload and learning/transfer: protect assistance capacity, address service barriers first and leave learning benefits unverified.

Librarians need bounded accepted duties and authority to defer review or omit practice.
Accountable reviewers need to distinguish technical behavior, supported actions and learning claims while preserving dissent.

Integrate both into a provisional operating card and separate practice material. Sequence 67 already implements the revision prompted by hypothetical objection 62; that draft change establishes neither practical protection nor approval. No new finding invalidates an earlier artifact. Human review, technical verification and field evidence remain pending.
objections: Hypothetical patron dissent: “I want help with the notice, not another exercise.”
Hypothetical librarian dissent: “Repeated checks add work we cannot sustain; defer review.”
Rivals include prompting, familiarity, obligation, language demands and clearer wording; demand, capacity, access arrangements and restoration remain unknown.
risks: Practice could become an informal prerequisite for assistance.
Stopping could be mistaken for concealing or clearing a draft.
Service and staffing barriers could be misrepresented as patron learning deficits.
system_capabilities: Keep activity, visibility and draft presence separate; stopping must not imply concealment or erasure.
Describe explicit fictional choices without sensitive-data entry, scores, tracking, assistance allocation or automatic handoffs.
Keep arrangement and evidence records outside the candidate, associated with exact revisions and configurations.
tradeoffs: Protecting assistance capacity may interrupt optional review.
Prompts support participation while limiting claims about uncued adaptation.
Minimal records protect discretion while limiting longitudinal inference.
